summary: Adversarially audit the blue-chip de-rating backtest across five lenses, then refute-check every material finding

findings.title: 58 corrupt adjDividend rows ARE the whole deep-entry edge; the rule's own trade set is unchanged
findings.where: pull.py:97-103 (dividend pull has no sanity filter); study.py:53-55 (DV built from every row) and :163-165 (dvd summed into exit proceeds); report.py:92-101 (portfolio mark/exit); variants.py:29-30 (walk2); final.py (charting leg gets dividends, survivorship leg gets divd=0.0)
findings.claim: fmp.dividend_calendar.adjDividend contains 58 rows across 8 symbols where the per-share dividend exceeds 20% of the PRIOR ADJUSTED CLOSE of the same stock: HINDPETRO 21 rows (worst Rs 1,314.93 against a Rs 204.23 close = 6.44x the entire share price), CUPID 14, ARVIND 9, DRREDDY 7 (Rs 1,727.64 against Rs 463.97), CESC 4, ANGELONE/STAR/TATAINVEST 1 each. study.py sums these into `dvd` and credits them to the holder as cash at exit. Three HINDPETRO episodes are credited 18.83x, 11.67x and 5.29x their entry price in 'dividends', turning price moves of +77%, +65% and +64% into net returns of +1956.3%, +1229.7% and +591.5%. Those three episodes alone are 161% of the published deep-bucket mean excess; ex-HINDPETRO the deep bucket is -26.6%, i.e. WORSE than the shallow band it is claimed to beat by 65pp. This is a point-in-time integrity failure rather than classic future-peeking: a retroactively-adjusted cash-flow series is credited at a scale no holder could ever have received, and on a share basis inconsistent with the adjusted price series the trade is priced in. Labelled hypothesis for the mechanism (not verified against FMP internals): corruption is confined to names with a bonus/split history and stops after each symbol's last corporate action (HINDPETRO rows become sane from 2025-08-14 at Rs 10.50), consistent with FMP applying a cumulative adjustment factor multiplicatively instead of dividing. Note the author's own final2.py (mtime 13:20, before RESULTS.md at 13:23) identified exactly these three HINDPETRO episodes and the 161% figure, but attributed them to metric choice (arithmetic vs annualised excess); the cause is the dividend rows, and RESULTS.md still headlines +41.4% and omits the annualised table entirely.
findings.direction: in favour of the rule
findings.magnitude: Destroys (a) and removes the (b)-rescue. Deep-bucket mean excess +41.4% -> -24.8% (58 rows dropped) / -34.8% (price-only); shallow -23.5% -> -24.5% / -30.1%; the deep-vs-shallow gap collapses from +64.9pp to -0.3pp / -4.7pp. On the author's own annualised metric the ordering INVERTS: deep median +10.6%/yr -> +5.2%/yr, now BELOW shallow's +6.4%/yr. All-entry mean excess -10.3% -> -24.6% / -31.1%. Portfolio: 20-slot hold-to-recovery 9.16% -> 6.87% / 5.35% CAGR vs NIFTYBEES 10.27% (shortfall -1.10pp -> -3.40pp / -4.92pp); 10-slot 11.48% (+1.21pp) -> 7.97% (-2.30pp) / 6.21% (-4.06pp), so the 10-slot book also loses to the index. RESULTS.md line 3 (the '36-month stop fixes it', Calmar 0.81) falls too: 36m-stop 10-slot 22.31% / +12.04pp / MDD -27.66% -> 10.47% / +0.20pp / MDD -45.90%; 20-slot 14.64% (+4.37pp) -> 7.89% (-2.38pp); episode-level 36m all-entry mean excess +11.4% -> -3.9%. The 20%-of-price filter is a LOWER bound on the correction (it is generous: HINDPETRO 2017-07-11 Rs 42.39 on a ~Rs 240 close survives it); price-only is the hard bound; truth sits between, nearer the filtered figure.
findings.empirical: Imported report.py/surv.py from the scratchpad and reproduced the published grid to the decimal (266/212/54 episodes; -10.3%/-23.5%/+41.4%; 36m row +11.4%/-0.3%/+57.4%; portfolio 11.48%/9.16%/22.31%/14.64%; closed 21/46/60/107). Trade set identical in every run (same entries, same exits, same 266 episodes, same closed counts), only credited cash moves, so this is not a sample change. findings.title: Asymmetric total-return accounting: stock leg credited dividends, NIFTYBEES credited none
findings.where: pull.py:81-84 (benchmark pull) vs :97-103 (dividend pull); study.py:163-168 (dvd added to the stock, bench is pure nb_c price return); RESULTS.md method table, row 'Dividends'
findings.claim: fmp.dividend_calendar has ZERO rows for NIFTYBEES.NS and NIFTYBEES.BO (verified by direct query against the warehouse), so `bench` in walk()/walk2()/mwalk2() is a pure price return while the charting stock leg adds cash dividends. RESULTS.md justifies the asymmetry with 'charting is price-only; NIFTYBEES reinvests, so without this the benchmark was favoured by the yield' - an assertion with no support in anything the study pulled. NIFTYBEES is itself a universe member, so it was in the dividend query's symbol list and simply returned nothing; the absence is a data gap, not evidence of accumulation. Compounding the inconsistency, the survivorship leg (mwalk2) already runs at divd=0.0, so the charting leg is the only one of the three return legs getting a yield. The 'price-only both legs' variant is therefore the only internally consistent comparison in the study.
findings.direction: in favour of the rule
findings.magnitude: Independent of the corrupt rows, the SANE dividend leg still moves the all-entry mean excess from -31.1% (price-only, internally consistent) to -24.6%, i.e. ~6.5pp of per-trade excess, and ~1.5pp of portfolio CAGR (20-slot 5.35% price-only vs 6.87% with sane dividends). Across the 253 charting episodes the leg adds 21.8pp to mean net (+58.9% -> +37.1%) over a 20-month median hold, i.e. ~2.2%/yr credited to the stock and 0%/yr to the index. The apples-to-apples anchor is the price-only result: all-entry mean excess -31.1%, 20-slot 5.35% CAGR vs 10.27%. If NIFTYBEES's real pre-2019 distributions were credited, the index leg would rise further (order 0.5-1.0pp CAGR) - not measurable from the cached data or from fmp.dividend_calendar.
findings.empirical: a6.py section 5 (NIFTYBEES in universe = True, 0 rows in divs.json, 0 in fund.json) plus a direct cr_client query of fmp.dividend_calendar for NIFTYBEES.NS/.BO returning 0 rows in b1.py's tail. a8.py variant C vs B isolates the sane-dividend contribution with the trade set held fixed; a9.py gives the portfolio pair (20-slot 6.87% vs 5.35%, 10-slot 7.97% vs 6.21%).
findings.short_summary: Stock leg gets dividends, benchmark gets none

audit.verdict_on_conclusion:
This lens challenges (a) and destroys it. (b) and (c) survive and are strengthened.

(a) IS AN ARTIFACT. The "+41.4% for <=-35% vs -23.5% for -25..-35%" split is produced by 58 corrupt adjDividend rows, 21 of them HINDPETRO. Drop only those rows and the deep bucket goes to -24.8% against the shallow band's -24.5% - the +64.9pp gap becomes -0.3pp. Price-only: -34.8% vs -30.1%, i.e. deep entries are WORSE. The author's own annualised metric inverts too (deep +10.6%/yr -> +5.2%/yr, below shallow's +6.4%/yr). Three HINDPETRO episodes supply 161% of the published deep mean; ex-HINDPETRO the deep bucket is -26.6%. The trade set is unchanged in every rerun - same 266 episodes, same entries and exits - so this is not a sample effect. RESULTS.md's line 3 ("a 2-3 year time stop fixes the whole-rule version", 36m 10-slot 22.31% CAGR / +12.04pp / Calmar 0.81) falls with it: +0.20pp vs the index and MDD -27.66% -> -45.90%.

(b) HOLDS AND HARDENS. Corrected, the 20-slot book returns 6.87% (filtered) / 5.35% (price-only) against NIFTYBEES 10.27% - the shortfall widens from -1.10pp to -3.40pp/-4.92pp - and the 10-slot book flips from +1.21pp to -2.30pp/-4.06pp, so no slot count beats the index. (c) HOLDS AND HARDENS: the 54 "favourable" episodes were never favourable, and the corrected drawdowns are worse than the index's (-32% to -50% vs -36.3%).

CHECKED AND CLEARED, no finding: the 730d lookback does reach into the pre-2011 raw-adjustment era (315/1,146 signals, 56/253 episodes have `hi` set by a pre-2011 bar, and that group's mean excess is -55.8% vs +13.4%), but the mechanism is falsified - all 7 episodes with an intervening split have splits dated 2011+ (ONGC 2011-02-08 2:1, TATAPOWER 2011-09-26 10:1, ASHOKLEY 2011-08-02 2:1, KTKBANK 2011-02-25) and the series shows no split-sized print (worst single-bar move 2010-2012 is -7.1%), so those bars are correctly adjusted. The -55.8% is the unbounded-arithmetic-excess artifact on four still-open PSU banks held the full 15.7 years (UCOBANK -436%, PNB -423%, UNIONBANK -390%, IDBI -377%), which the author already discloses as censoring.

VERIFIED CLEAN - every mechanical point-in-time check passes with zero violations, re-measured independently: the 2-year-high window is exactly (t-730d, t], recomputed from scratch with 0/1,146 mismatches, includes the decision bar's own high and never a later bar; the signal price equals the close of the decision bar in 1,146/1,146 and a stock must print on t to qualify; entry is the first bar strictly after t in walk(), walk2() AND the portfolio fill map (0/1,146 violations, median lag 2 calendar days, max 5; 0/186 fill days on or before their decision date); nifty_off_high(t) is strictly backward (0/186); the universe SQL window [t-372d, t-2d) is strictly past and conservatively ends two days early, with rank and days_traded>=180 both point-in-time; the CA level-shift detector's 5-bar recovery test never touches a post-decision bar for any actual signal (0/1,146 have a shift within 5 bars of t); the "two fiscal years earlier" lookup is exactly 2.000 years of period-end gap in 1,146/1,146 signals (max 2.003), with 0 mixed fiscalYear conventions and 0 duplicate (symbol, period_end) rows, and the FY-2 baseline is drawn from the already-available set so it can never be unpublished; the 120-day EPS lag is ~2x SEBI LODR Reg 33's 60-day annual deadline so its direction is conservative, the statement actually used is at most 1.25 years old, and the result is stable across LAG = 60/90/120/180d (256/257/253/249 episodes, median excess +15.1/+14.2/+14.0/+11.8%) - the residual exposure is late filers, which the positive-net-income and top-150-turnover gates largely exclude, and real Indian filing dates are unmeasurable from this data; and FMP's eps IS split-restated onto the adjusted price series' share basis (eps == ni/shs at median ratio 1.0000; SBIN FY2005 eps 9.8 not the as-reported Rs 81.8, EICHERMOT FY2004 1.2 not Rs 12), with only 23 share-basis breaks matching a real split across 382 symbols and 0/1,146 signals using an eps row off-basis by more than 10% (max 1.04), so pe_now and pe_need are NOT contaminated by post-decision splits.

Durable record: scratchpad/AUDIT_LOOKAHEAD_FINDINGS.txt; measurement scripts a0-a9, b1-b2.py in the same directory; fmp.splits_calendar for the 450 universe symbols newly cached at bcbt/uni_splits.json (578 events).

verdict.reasoning:
The DATA DEFECT IS REAL and the claim's numbers are exact — I could not refute a single one. But the claim's indictment of the deliverable is STALE, and the defect moves none of the three conclusions as they now stand.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (independently, from divs.json + the px_*.json panel):
- 58 rows across exactly 8 symbols have adjDividend > 20% of the prior adjusted close, with exactly the claimed per-symbol counts: HINDPETRO 21, CUPID 14, ARVIND 9, DRREDDY 7, CESC 4, STAR/TATAINVEST/ANGELONE 1 each.
- Worst rows match: HINDPETRO 2021-07-08 Rs 1,314.93 vs a Rs 189.23 prior close (6.95x); DRREDDY 2018-07-16 Rs 1,727.64 vs Rs 418.79 (4.13x). (The claim's Rs 204.23 / Rs 463.97 denominators differ slightly from my prior-close values but the ratios are the same order.)
- Those rows carry 25.4% of all dividend rupee value in the pull. Sane rows: median 0.67%, p95 3.88%, max 19.78% — so the 58 are a clean, separable tail, not a continuum.
- HINDPETRO rows become sane from 2025-08-14 (Rs 10.50 = 2.7%), consistent with the claimed cumulative-factor mechanism.
- pull.py:97-103 has no sanity filter (only adjDividend > 0). study.py:53-55 builds DV from every row and :163-165 sums it into exit proceeds. variants.py:29-30 and fixed.py:93 do the same. Confirmed by reading.
- Three HINDPETRO episodes are credited 18.83x / 11.67x / 5.29x their entry price and print net +1956.3% / +1229.7% / +591.5%; price-only they are +76.4% / +64.8% / +63.5%. CESC 2018-12-03 is a fourth at 1.18x. Exactly 4 of 462 charting episodes get dvd > 1x entry.
- Not a sample change: with dividends dropped the candidate set and episode keys are byte-identical (462 episodes, assert on the key set passed). Only credited cash moves. The auditor's framing is right.

WHY IT IS NOT FATAL AND MOVES NOTHING:
The deliverable on disk has already been rewritten to fix this. studies/bluechip_derating/RESULTS.md has mtime 13:53, not the 13:23 the claim describes. The current version:
- lists "fmp.dividend_calendar.adjDividend is corrupt for NSE" as data defect #1, quotes the HINDPETRO Rs 1,314.93 row and the 25.3% value share, and states "HINDPETRO was the largest single contributor to what I had reported as a deep-entry edge, so that edge was this defect";
- retracts the +41.4% deep-bucket claim in full under "Retractions", naming this defect as one of four causes;
- marks study.py / report.py / variants.py / final.py as superseded with "Do not quote their output";
- computes its headline portfolio table from nodiv.py, which drops exactly these 58 rows (its log prints "sanitised dividends: dropped 58 corrupt rows"). I re-ran nodiv.py and it reproduces to the decimal.
So the claim's two assertions about the artifact — that RESULTS.md "still headlines +41.4%" and "omits the annualised table entirely" — are both false of the file as it exists.

On the three conclusions, measured:
(a) "edge only in deep entries" is NOT a standing conclusion — RESULTS.md says "Buying deeper is worse, not better. Deep-only is the single worst arm, -3.52pp." Fixing dividends keeps it rejected (deep-only 20 slots: -3.52pp price-only, -2.30pp sanitised, and the per-episode deep bucket still carries p10 net -89.8% and 71% recovery over a median 35 months).
(b) "held-to-recovery does not beat NIFTYBEES" is stated on the already-clean numbers: -2.10pp at 20 slots price-only, -0.81pp sanitised, +0.98pp/+2.53pp at 10 slots on 26 closed trades in 15.7y. Unmoved.
(c) "not a safe alpha for real money" — unmoved and strengthened. Every dividend correction moves against the rule.

Worth noting for the record: the defect WAS decisive, and the author's own fix is what makes (b) true. With raw dividends the portfolio beat the index at both slot counts (+6.18pp at 10, +1.36pp at 20, fixed_pf.log); price-only it is +0.98pp and -2.10pp. So the claimed direction "in favour of the rule" is right — it just no longer reaches the published numbers.

GENUINE RESIDUAL (real, new, non-material): the published 511-episode per-episode table comes from fixed_run.py, which runs the survivorship leg with divs=False (line 81) but the charting leg with the default divs=True (line 98). That table is therefore dividend-asymmetric and inconsistent with the price-only headline portfolio. I isolated the effect: removing ONLY the 58 corrupt rows moves it by at most 1.76pp/yr (deep medAnnEx +12.8 -> +11.1%/yr; deep medNet +75.6 -> +74.7%; the headline "all" row +9.5 -> +9.3%/yr, beat 67% -> 67%, p10 and recovery% and medMo all unchanged). The larger shift to +6.5%/yr and 62% comes from dropping legitimate dividends too, which is a conservative methodological choice, not corruption. So RESULTS.md's "median annualised excess ~+9.5%/yr, beats the index 67%" is overstated by ~0.2pp/yr by the corruption and by ~3pp/yr by the dividend-treatment inconsistency — worth a one-line fix (make fixed_run.py:98 pass divs=False, or publish the sanitised column), but it flips nothing. Medians are robust to 4 contaminated episodes in 462; the means are destroyed, and RESULTS.md quotes no means in that table and explicitly instructs "Use median annualised excess."

Verdict: defect real, severity overstated (not fatal — already remediated in the shipped artifact), moves none of (a), (b), (c).
verdict.which_conclusion: None. (a) is already retracted in the current RESULTS.md with this very defect named as a cause, and the fix keeps it retracted (deep-only is the worst arm at -3.52pp). (b) and (c) are already computed on dividend-free prices (nodiv.py) and every dividend correction strengthens them. Had the deliverable still been the 13:16/13:20 pass, the defect would have moved both (a) and (b) — with raw dividends the portfolio beat the index at 10 and 20 slots (+6.18pp / +1.36pp) versus +0.98pp / -2.10pp price-only — but that pass is marked superseded and "do not quote".

verdict.reasoning:
REAL BUT MIS-CHARACTERISED, AND IMMATERIAL. I set refuted=false only because the mechanical asymmetry is positively confirmable: in fixed.py `walk()` takes `divs=True` by default so the charting leg adds cash dividends, fixed_run.py `surv_eps()` calls it with `divs=False`, and `bench` is a bare `nb_c[bj]/nb_c[bi]-1` with no dividend accrual. The claim's three substantive assertions — direction, severity, and remedy — are all refuted by measurement.

1. "bench is a pure price return" is WRONG over most of the window. NIFTYBEES/^NSEI drifts +0.79%/yr across 2011-01→2026-10 (ratio 0.010096 → 0.011427, rising in 14 of 15 calendar years), i.e. the benchmark series already carries ~60% of the index yield. By era: 2011-2015 +0.02%/yr (distributing — persistent ratio step-downs at 2012-03-09 -1.13%, 2013-03-12 -0.94%, 2014-03-10 -1.26%, 2015-02-19 -0.86%, all annual and all absent after 2015) vs 2016-2026 +1.11%/yr (accumulating, monotone). So the asymmetry is real for roughly the first third of the window and essentially absent for the last two thirds. The study's "NIFTYBEES reinvests" assertion was unsupported by anything it pulled (fair process criticism) but is substantively TRUE and now measured; the claim's inference that "the absence is a data gap, not evidence of accumulation" is correct about the evidence and wrong about the fact. Residual unjustified bias = realised stock-leg yield minus the 0.79%/yr the bench already retains, i.e. ~0.3-0.6pp/yr, not the full yield the claim implies.

2. Direction is BACKWARDS for the published headline. RESULTS.md's headline portfolio table IS the nodiv.py NODIV arm — no dividends on any leg — which is exactly the claim's own "only internally consistent comparison". The alleged material bias in favour of the rule is therefore absent from the numbers the verdict rests on; that arm is biased AGAINST the rule by the dividends it drops (1.30pp of CAGR at 20 slots, 1.55pp at 10). The dividend-inclusive arm (SANITISED) is reported alongside and labelled. The claim's point 5 (mwalk2 at divd=0.0) is also conservative, not favourable: those are the names marked to zero at NCLT, and crediting them dividends can only improve the rule — I ran it (SAN surv leg) and it moves all-bucket median annualised excess by +0.1pp.

3. Nothing moves, under ANY treatment. Since vs-idx = strategy CAGR − bench CAGR, a bench bump g shifts every published cell by exactly −g. I tabulated g ∈ {0, 0.32 (measured leak = 1.11 − 0.79), 0.61 (leak if gross yield were 1.40%), 1.30 (the claim's own maximal assumption: bench has no dividends at all)}. (a) deep-only-20 is the worst arm in every one of the 8 columns (−2.30pp to −4.82pp), so "the edge is only in deep entries" stays dead and deep stays worst. (b) hold-to-recovery at 20 slots loses in all 8 cells (−0.81 to −3.41pp); 10 slots wins +0.98 to +2.53 on 26 closed trades in 15.7 years, which RESULTS.md already calls noise. The single sign change anywhere in the grid is 10-slot NODIV at the claim's own g=1.30 (+0.98 → −0.32pp), which moves TOWARD "does not beat NIFTYBEES" — it strengthens (b), it cannot flip it. (c) untouched: the dividend leg does not change MDD at all (−32.3% to −59.7% strategy vs −36.3% index), and p10 net gets WORSE price-only (−24.8% → −30.1% overall, deep −88.8% → −89.8%).

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND, flagged not folded in: fixed_run.py's event-study loop (which is verbatim RESULTS.md's per-episode table) runs the RAW dividend map, including the HINDPETRO 2021-07-08 ₹1,314.93 row — confirmed present in DV as loaded — while the same document's method table says "Dividends: not trusted" and its defect #1 calls the field corrupt. Re-running sanitised: all-bucket median annualised excess +9.5 → +9.3%/yr, beat 67% → 67%, DEEP +12.8 → +11.1%/yr; price-only both legs +9.5 → +6.5%/yr, beat 67% → 62%, DEEP +12.8 → +10.1%/yr. The "signal carries information per episode" statement survives both, and deep stays per-episode better than shallow in all four treatments, so this is a consistency/documentation fix, not a conclusion change.

DOC FIX recommended (no conclusion change): RESULTS.md ll.27-28 and nodiv.py's docstring assert "NIFTYBEES reinvests, so NODIV understates the rule by ~1.5%/yr". Measured, the NODIV understatement relative to a true total-return-vs-total-return comparison is (1.30-1.55pp realised strategy yield) − (0.32-0.61pp bench leak) ≈ 0.7-1.2pp/yr, and the 2011-2015 distributing era should be stated rather than the blanket "reinvests".

audit.verdict_on_conclusion:
This lens CHALLENGES (a) and STRENGTHENS (b) and (c).

(a) is the casualty. "+41.4% mean excess for the deep bucket, 54 episodes" does not survive. The survivorship correction leg itself is crippled by two compounding defects (F1): a dead market-wide guard caused by a 19,800s epoch mismatch between bhavcopy and charting, and a −8% level-shift detector run on UNADJUSTED bhavcopy prices whose window truncation kills 66.7% of missing-name universe slots versus 43.1% on the adjusted charting leg. Fixing them takes the shipped survivorship leg from 35 episodes / 13 kept failures to 85 / 39, and the names it restores are precisely the ones RESULTS.md itself names as "exactly the names that matter" — HDIL, DHFL, EDUCOMP, OPTOCIRCUI, ARSSINFRA, IBREALEST, IBULHSGFIN. Deep-bucket mean excess ladder: +41.4% as shipped → +34.9% (epoch bug alone) → +7.3% (symmetric, CA handling off on both legs — the apples-to-apples figure) → −4.6% (charting truncate + surv splits-only). The deep-minus-shallow gap falls from +64.9pp to +19.3pp, and the beat-rate advantage INVERTS (deep 69% vs shallow 62% → deep 64% vs shallow 66%). Deep recovery rate falls from 76% to 73%/64% against shallow's 82%. Note the write-up's own preferred statistic survives: median excess +26.3% → +30.1% symmetric. So "the edge lives entirely in deep entries" is trimmed to "deep entries have a better median, no better frequency, and a mean that is an artefact of six very large winners and of failures the code could not see."

(b) is strengthened but for a different reason than stated. The 20-slot 9.16% vs 10.27% comparison is computed on a survivor-only price panel (F2): portfolio()/pf() build their price lookup from the 338 charting symbols, so the 112 absentees — 17.1% of universe slots overall and 36.6% in 2011 — can never be filled, and the sim's deepest-first ranking by upside concentrates it in exactly the names it cannot see. Making the absentees fillable: 20-slot hold-to-recovery −1.10pp → −1.91pp (−2.19pp using the study's own detector); 20-slot 36-month stop +4.37pp → +2.10pp (+3.17pp lower bound); and the write-up's star figure, 10-slot 36-month stop at 22.31% CAGR / MDD −27.66% / +12.04pp, becomes 18.68% / +8.41pp on the study's own detector and 6.74% / MDD −62.23% / −3.53pp with the detector fixed. Six realised wipeouts (EDUCOMP −100%, HDIL −100%, DHFL −100%, SINTEX −99%, RELCAPITAL −97%, RCOM −80%) appear only in the full-universe runs. RESULTS.md calls the portfolio sim "the behavioural truth" while leaving it entirely uncorrected.

(c) is strengthened. The favourable slice is thinner and weaker than reported, drawdown is worse not better (the corrected 10-slot 36m run shows MDD −62% vs the index's −36%), and 53 further symbols / 907 slots clear the price trigger before dying at an FMP-fundamentals gate that cannot even be evaluated (F3), so the true failure count is unmeasured, not bounded.

VERIFIED, do not re-raise: (1) the CLOSE*VOLUME-for-TURNOVER substitution holds in every year 2011–2024, not just 2023 — top-100 overlap 99.2–100/100, rank correlation 0.995–1.000 (caveat: ranks 100–150 and 2025–26 are unvalidated). (2) "112 of 450 symbols, 17.1% of slots" is exactly right (4,768/27,900 = 17.09%). (3) Universe-entry endogeneity is NOT the explanation — restricted to entries where persistence is measurable (≥2013-01), 24/24-month-persistent episodes average +15.5% excess versus +21.6% for non-persistent, i.e. the effect reverses, and 25 of the 39 restored failures WERE in the top 150 for all 24 prior months (DHFL, RCOM, SINTEX, RELCAPITAL, IBREALEST, HDIL, RELINFRA). The "blue chip" proxy is defensible as "large and liquid"; it is simply not a solvency screen. (4) JETAIRWAYS and JPASSOCIAT are excluded legitimately (loss-making / no EPS growth across two FYs), not by a data hole. (5) No charting symbol has a frozen series (0 of 338). (6) The surv leg's divd=0.0 omits only 1.7% of entry price on average — immaterial.

findings.title: The survivorship-correction leg's level-shift detector hides two-thirds of the failure episodes: a dead market guard (epoch mismatch) plus a -8% detector run on unadjusted prices
findings.claim: surv.py's MSH loop calls NB_RET.get(int(d[i]), 0.0) to skip market-wide crash days, but bhavcopy date_epoch is offset +19,800s (05:30) from charting/NIFTYBEES epochs, so the lookup hits 0 of 4,215 dates and the guard NEVER fires. Separately the same -8% detector runs on UNADJUSTED bhavcopy closes while the charting leg runs on adjusted ones. Every flagged day truncates the 2-year high window (w0 = max(w0, max(sh))), which then fails MIN_BARS=400. Net effect: 3,181 of 4,768 missing-name universe slots (66.7%) die at MIN_BARS purely because of truncation, versus 43.1% on the charting leg. The defence that dying names have more real corporate actions is refuted: the drop-size distribution of detector-only days is near-identical on the two legs (median -10.0% both; share <=-30% 4.6% surv vs 3.4% charting), and real splits are already masked separately from fmp.splits_calendar. The extra damage is simply that collapsing names have more -8% days (13.6/symbol vs 8.5), which is the survivorship-amplifying mechanism, not a justification. The restored names are the ones RESULTS.md itself calls 'exactly the names that matter'.
findings.direction: In favour of the rule. Every headline is biased up; conclusion (a)'s deep-bucket figure is the main casualty.
findings.magnitude: Survivorship leg: 35 episodes / 13 kept failures -> 85 / 39. DEEP-bucket mean excess over NIFTYBEES: +41.4% as shipped -> +34.9% (epoch bug fixed alone) -> +10.1% (-15% detector) -> +4.5% (-20% detector) -> +7.3% (symmetric, CA handling off on BOTH legs, n=135) -> -4.6% (charting truncate + surv splits-only, n=67). Deep-minus-shallow gap +64.9pp -> +19.3pp. Beat-rate advantage inverts: deep 69% vs shallow 62% -> deep 64% vs shallow 66%. Deep recovery 76% -> 73%/64% vs shallow 82%. Median excess is robust (+26.3% -> +30.1% symmetric), so the write-up's own preferred statistic survives while the mean, which is how claim (a) is stated, does not.
findings.empirical: audit/a3.py A6 (NB_RET hit rate 0/4215; charting 100%); a4.py A8 (dominant offset 19800s, fixed-map hit rate 4211/4215) and A9 (as_shipped 35 eps / fixed_guard 37 / splits_only 85, with the 27 new episodes listed); a3.py A5 (MIN_BARS cause split: surv TRUNC_CAUSED 3181 vs genuinely_sparse 153; charting 9961 vs 367); a6.py A12 (the full detector-threshold ladder) and A13 (only 1 post-entry split among the 39 restored, IBULHSGFIN 2024-02-01, immaterial); a11.py A23 (drop-size histograms) and A24 (symmetric ca_mode=off on both legs: deep n=135 meanExc +7.3%, medExc +30.1%, beat 64%, recov 73%).
findings.where: backtest/surv.py lines 28-40 (MSH construction: NB_RET.get on bhavcopy epochs, -0.08 threshold on unadjusted closes) and lines 63-66 (w0 truncation + the 400-bar gate); same logic duplicated in final.py lines 44-47.
findings.short_summary: Dead market guard + unadjusted-price detector hide 2/3 of failures

findings.title: The portfolio simulation is 100% uncorrected for survivorship, and its deepest-first ranking concentrates it in exactly the names it cannot see
findings.claim: portfolio() in report.py and pf() in variants.py build their price lookup as pxc={s:... for s in S}, i.e. only from the 338 charting symbols. The 112 charting-absent universe members - 17.1% of all universe slots and 36.6% of 2011 slots - can never be filled, so no portfolio run ever holds RCOM, SINTEX, RELCAPITAL, HDIL, DHFL, EDUCOMP, OPTOCIRCUI, IBREALEST (or TATAMOTORS and HDFC on the winning side). Worse, both sims sort candidates by -up (deepest discount first), which is precisely the ordering that fills the deepest-fallen names first - and the deepest-fallen are disproportionately the absentees. So the deepest-first ranking that produces the headline '+12.04pp' is the ranking that maximises exposure to the invisible set. RESULTS.md acknowledges the bias for the episode table ('the bias that is NOT yet in those numbers') and then presents the portfolio table with no correction at all, while calling the portfolio sim 'the behavioural truth'.
findings.direction: In favour of the rule. All portfolio CAGRs and Calmars are biased up and the max drawdowns biased toward zero.
findings.magnitude: Making the 112 absentees fillable from bhavcopy. LOWER BOUND, using the study's own (broken) detector so only the 204 candidate slots it would itself have found: 10-slot 36-month stop 22.31% CAGR / +12.04pp -> 18.68% / +8.41pp; 20-slot 36m +4.37pp -> +3.17pp; 20-slot hold-to-recovery -1.10pp -> -2.19pp. With the detector fixed: 10-slot 36m -> 6.74% CAGR, MDD -27.66% -> -62.23%, Calmar 0.81 -> 0.11, +12.04pp -> -3.53pp; 20-slot 36m 14.64% -> 12.37% (+2.10pp); 20-slot hold-to-recovery 9.16% -> 8.36% (-1.91pp); 10-slot hold-to-recovery 11.48% -> 8.30% (+1.21pp -> -1.97pp). Terminal-mark treatment is almost irrelevant (no-haircut variant 7.28% vs 6.74%), so the damage is the price path, not the recovery assumption. Realised wipeouts appear only in the full-universe runs: EDUCOMP -100%, HDIL -100%, DHFL -100%, SINTEX -99%, RELCAPITAL -97%, RCOM -80%.
findings.empirical: audit/a10.py A21 (shipped vs full-universe portfolio grid, 10/20 slots x hold-to-recovery/36m) and A22 (lower bound on the study's own detector; generous no-haircut variant). Shipped baselines reproduced exactly from variants.log/main.log (11.48/9.16/22.31/14.64%).
findings.where: backtest/report.py line 88 (pxc built from S only) and variants.py line 48 (same), with the deepest-first fill at report.py line 81 / variants.py line 42 (sort key -up).
findings.short_summary: Portfolio sim can only ever hold the 338 survivors

findings.title: 53 symbols and 907 universe slots clear the -25%-off-high trigger and are then silently dropped because fmp.income_statement has no FY rows for them
findings.claim: mlatest_fy() returns (None, None) when FMP carries no FY income statement for a symbol, and the caller does a bare `continue`. On the charting leg this gate costs 1 slot of 23,132 (0.004%). On the missing-name leg it costs 216 slots / 22 symbols under the shipped detector, and 907 slots / 53 symbols once the detector stops killing them earlier at MIN_BARS. 51 of the 53 have exactly ZERO FY rows with an EPS. The list is the Indian insolvency roll: IVRCLINFRA, LITL (Lanco Infratech), AMTEKAUTO, BHUSANSTL, ALOKTEXT, GITANJALI, KFA (Kingfisher), ABGSHIP, ORCHIDCHEM, PIPAVAVYD, FRL (Future Retail), EVERONN, SATYAMCOMP, FINANTECH (NSEL), HANUNG, ISPATIND - plus the bank amalgamations (ORIENTBANK 75 slots, ALBK 55, DENABANK 41, ANDHRABANK, SYNDIBANK, VIJAYABANK, IDFCBANK) which the study would drop anyway. So fmp.income_statement is itself a survivor-biased panel for India, and the survivorship correction inherits that bias at the gate it cannot evaluate. These episodes are unmeasured, not bounded: the 'BOUND: every unverified ticker treated as a TOTAL LOSS' arm in merge2.py cannot reach them because they never become candidates.
findings.direction: In favour of the rule. The uncovered names are dead companies, so excluding them removes failures only.
findings.magnitude: Estimated 20-45 additional failure episodes - 2-3x the 13 the study folded in - from 907 trigger-passing slots x the visible leg's 35.6% pass rate through the fundamentals gates (1,146 of 3,219 slots that reach them) / 6.9 candidate slots per episode on the survivorship leg. Roughly half the 53 are amalgamations the study would drop, so call it 10-25 net kept failures. Not folded into my restated numbers above, so every deep-bucket figure I quote is still an upper bound.
findings.empirical: audit/a9.py A18 (53 symbols with slot counts, last EQ bar and FMP FY row counts, after the splits-only detector stops truncating); a2.py A4 (the two side-by-side funnels: 5_NO_FMP_FUNDAMENTALS 216/4,768 = 4.5% on the missing leg vs 1/23,132 = 0.0% on the visible leg; PASS rates 4.3% vs 5.0%).

findings.short_summary: 907 trigger-passing slots die at a missing-FMP gate

findings.title: 'Dropping renames is conservative' is justified with NET returns while the headline metric is EXCESS, where it is backwards for the shallow bucket - and 14 of the 22 dropped episodes had already closed before the rename
findings.claim: merge2.py's docstring defends dropping RENAME/MERGER_SHARE_SWAP/DEMERGER by citing net returns ('TATAMOTORS +36.6%, HDFC +21.4%, SRTRANSFIN +38.9%, CADILAHC +58.7%'). But the headline table reports EXCESS over NIFTYBEES, and in excess terms the 15 dropped SHALLOW episodes average -92.5% (TATAMOTORS +38.7% net is -112.4% excess; IDFC -436.6%) while only the 7 dropped DEEP episodes are winners (+29.4%). So the drop removes losers from the shallow bucket, which flatters it. Second issue: the drop is applied per symbol, not per episode. 14 of the 22 dropped episodes are CLOSED - the stock regained its frozen 2-year high and the position exited YEARS before the rename (CADILAHC x3, CENTURYTEX x2, SRTRANSFIN x3, TATAMOTORS x2, TATAMTRDVR x3, AMARAJABAT). Those are fully measured, unambiguous outcomes thrown away. Third: the successors are all in the charting panel (HDFCBANK, LTIM, SHRIRAMFIN, ZYDUSLIFE, TATACONSUM, CGPOWER, IDFCFIRSTB), so the true holder path through a rename was measurable and simply was not measured - most consequentially TATAMOTORS, absent for 181 of 186 universe months, whose 2018-2020 de-rating and recovery is the decade's largest instance of the pattern under test.
findings.direction: Against the rule on the shallow bucket (the shipped -23.5% is too harsh), in favour on the deep bucket. Net direction on claim (b) is against the rule, i.e. the write-up's conservatism claim is wrong in sign but happens to support its own conclusion.
findings.magnitude: Including all 22 dropped at their raw bhavcopy marks: all-entry mean excess -10.3% -> -13.6%, shallow -23.5% -> -28.1%, DEEP +41.4% -> +40.0% (gap widens slightly). Restoring only the 14 closed episodes, where the rename post-dates the exit and no judgement is needed: all -10.3% -> about -10.5%, deep -> about +42.9%, shallow -> about -24.8%. Small in magnitude; the defect is that the stated justification does not hold in the reported metric.

findings.title: Excess return is never horizon-normalised, and every survivorship correction is an open-ended position, so the correction's magnitude is a horizon artefact
findings.claim: walk()/surv_episodes() compute excess as net minus the benchmark's total return over the identical calendar window, with no annualisation and no cap on the window. Holding periods in the corrected sample span 38 to 5,729 days. Because a survivorship failure by definition never reaches its target, every kept failure is 'open' and is marked at the last bar, so each one draws the maximum-length benchmark leg: RELINFRA 2011-02-28 to 2025-06-03 is 5,209 days, net -38.7% against a benchmark of +394.5%, giving an 'excess' of -433.1%; BGRENERGY -424.5% over 5,442 days; five SINTEX episodes between -219% and -236%. 46 of the 266 corrected episodes have |excess| > 100% and they account for 209% of the sum of all excesses. So both the deep bucket's +41.4% (driven up by a handful of multi-year compounders) and the size of the survivorship haircut (driven down by six maximal-horizon failures) are artefacts of mixing 6-month and 15-year holds in one arithmetic mean. The write-up half-sees this ('the mean/median split is the whole story') but still states claim (a) in means.
findings.direction: Unclear in sign; it amplifies the magnitude of every mean-excess number in both directions and makes the deep-vs-shallow comparison non-comparable, since deep entries take a median 27.7 months versus 20.1 for shallow.
findings.magnitude: Mechanically large. The 13 kept failures move the deep bucket by -28.5pp (+69.9% -> +41.4%) and the shallow bucket by only -4.5pp (-19.0% -> -23.5%), and that asymmetry is driven by holding-period length rather than by severity. A per-trade annualised or horizon-matched excess would shrink the spread between the buckets; report.py already computes a per-trade annualised figure and the mean there is +128.6% (+561,836.6% on the overlapping-signal sample), which shows the metric is unusable as written.
findings.empirical: audit/a5.py A11 (per-episode entry/exit/days/net/bench/excess for all 13 kept failures; holding-period spread 38-5,729 days; 46/266 episodes with |excess|>100% contributing 209% of the excess sum); derived bucket decomposition base deep +69.9% -> +41.4% from a5.py A10.

findings.title: Charting coverage of the universe is a steep time gradient (36.6% missing in 2011 falling to 0.2% in 2026), not the flat 17.1% the write-up reports
findings.claim: The headline '112 of 450 universe symbols are absent, 17.1% of all universe slots' is exactly right in aggregate (4,768 of 27,900 = 17.09%) but it averages over a monotone gradient that is the survivorship mechanism itself: nse_charting_day covers currently-listed names, so coverage is near-perfect at the end of the window and worst at the start. Missing slots by year: 36.6% (2011), 31.2, 29.2, 24.4, 24.6, 22.1, 20.3, 18.7, 15.9, 12.1, 9.2, 8.4, 5.3, 4.4, 2.3, 0.2% (2026). The effective selection pool was 95 names in 2011 and 150 in 2026. This matters for one specific claim: the 2011 cohort - 45 of 253 episodes, the worst in the table (median excess -10.4%, median drawdown-first -38.8%) and the one RESULTS.md calls 'the cautionary cohort and the closest analogue to today' - was selected from 63% of the stated universe, with the other 37% being a mix of the decade's biggest failures and biggest renamed winners. The gradient also means the backtest's early years are maximally biased while its recent years are nearly clean, so any time-series read of the rule's decay is confounded.
findings.direction: In favour of the rule, strongly concentrated in the early window. It also understates how much of the 2011 'analogue' cohort is unobserved.
findings.magnitude: The 2011 and 2012 cohorts (63 of 253 episodes) were drawn from pools of 95 and 103 names against a nominal 150. Seven of the 39 restored failures have entry dates in the censored 2011-2012 stretch. No clean single-number restatement, but it is the reason the 2011 cohort cannot be used as the 'today analogue' the write-up makes it.
findings.empirical: audit/a2.py A3 (per-year slots/missing/missing%/visible pool); first bash measurement (per-date missing counts: 56/150 at 2011-01-31, 27/150 at 2018-10-31, 0/150 at 2026-06-30; top missing by months-in-universe: TATAMOTORS 181, HDFC 153, MCDOWELL-N 152, SRTRANSFIN 147, IBREALEST 136).

findings.title: delisted() is uninformative for all 112 symbols, bhavcopy ends 2026-03-24 so the survivorship leg's forward walk is 6.5 months shorter than the charting leg's, and bhavcopy is EQ-series only
findings.claim: Three small data-boundary defects, grouped. (1) surv.py computes DATA_END = max(nb_d[-1], max(LAST)) = max(2026-10-09, 2026-03-24) = 2026-10-09 because nse_bhavcopy_historical ends 2026-03-24 while charting runs to 2026-10-09, so delisted() - LAST[s] < DATA_END - 200 days - returns True for every one of the 112 symbols, including RELINFRA (last bar 2025-06-03 at 380.60), ABAN (2025-09-03), BGRENERGY (2026-02-22) and RAJESHEXPO (2025-12-23), all of which are live NSE stocks. The flag is only used to annotate trades, not to set the haircut in merge2.py/final.py, so it is headline-neutral, but it means the triage that produced the classifications ran on a predicate that is constant-True. (2) Four decision dates (2026-03-30 through 2026-06-30) have no bhavcopy data at all, and every open survivorship position is marked 6.5 months earlier than its charting counterpart - a small asymmetry in the open-position marks that feed the corrected table. (3) nse_bhavcopy_historical carries exactly one series (SERIES='EQ', 9,646,965 rows, 5,072 symbols, 1994-11-02 to 2026-03-24), so the SERIES='EQ' filter in pull.py and pull_surv.py is a no-op - but it also means any period a distressed name spent in BE/trade-for-trade surveillance is simply absent from the table rather than filtered, which is an invisible coverage truncation ahead of exactly the deaths the correction is trying to capture.
findings.direction: Mostly neutral for the headline. The truncated forward walk marks failures slightly earlier (direction ambiguous); the invisible BE periods bias in favour of the rule by shortening the observed decline.
findings.magnitude: Headline-neutral as coded. Worth stating because the classification triage leaned on delisted(), and because item (3) means no amount of work on this table can see a pre-delisting surveillance period.
findings.empirical: audit/a9.py A20 (DATA_END 2026-10-09, threshold 2026-03-23, delisted()==False for [] i.e. zero of 112; the four orphan decision dates); q1.py (bhavcopy span 1994-11-02 to 2026-03-24, 5,072 symbols, nser=1; series mix EQ only; per-symbol EQ spans and last closes for the 19 key names).

finding.title: The survivorship-correction leg's level-shift detector hides two-thirds of the failure episodes: a dead market guard (epoch mismatch) plus a -8% detector run on unadjusted prices
finding.claim: surv.py's MSH loop calls NB_RET.get(int(d[i]), 0.0) to skip market-wide crash days, but bhavcopy date_epoch is offset +19,800s (05:30) from charting/NIFTYBEES epochs, so the lookup hits 0 of 4,215 dates and the guard NEVER fires. Separately the same -8% detector runs on UNADJUSTED bhavcopy closes while the charting leg runs on adjusted ones. Every flagged day truncates the 2-year high window (w0 = max(w0, max(sh))), which then fails MIN_BARS=400. Net effect: 3,181 of 4,768 missing-name universe slots (66.7%) die at MIN_BARS purely because of truncation, versus 43.1% on the charting leg. The defence that dying names have more real corporate actions is refuted: the drop-size distribution of detector-only days is near-identical on the two legs (median -10.0% both; share <=-30% 4.6% surv vs 3.4% charting), and real splits are already masked separately from fmp.splits_calendar. The extra damage is simply that collapsing names have more -8% days (13.6/symbol vs 8.5), which is the survivorship-amplifying mechanism, not a justification. The restored names are the ones RESULTS.md itself calls 'exactly the names that matter'.
finding.direction: In favour of the rule. Every headline is biased up; conclusion (a)'s deep-bucket figure is the main casualty.
finding.magnitude: Survivorship leg: 35 episodes / 13 kept failures -> 85 / 39. DEEP-bucket mean excess over NIFTYBEES: +41.4% as shipped -> +34.9% (epoch bug fixed alone) -> +10.1% (-15% detector) -> +4.5% (-20% detector) -> +7.3% (symmetric, CA handling off on BOTH legs, n=135) -> -4.6% (charting truncate + surv splits-only, n=67). Deep-minus-shallow gap +64.9pp -> +19.3pp. Beat-rate advantage inverts: deep 69% vs shallow 62% -> deep 64% vs shallow 66%. Deep recovery 76% -> 73%/64% vs shallow 82%. Median excess is robust (+26.3% -> +30.1% symmetric), so the write-up's own preferred statistic survives while the mean, which is how claim (a) is stated, does not.
finding.empirical: audit/a3.py A6 (NB_RET hit rate 0/4215; charting 100%); a4.py A8 (dominant offset 19800s, fixed-map hit rate 4211/4215) and A9 (as_shipped 35 eps / fixed_guard 37 / splits_only 85, with the 27 new episodes listed); a3.py A5 (MIN_BARS cause split: surv TRUNC_CAUSED 3181 vs genuinely_sparse 153; charting 9961 vs 367); a6.py A12 (the full detector-threshold ladder) and A13 (only 1 post-entry split among the 39 restored, IBULHSGFIN 2024-02-01, immaterial); a11.py A23 (drop-size histograms) and A24 (symmetric ca_mode=off on both legs: deep n=135 meanExc +7.3%, medExc +30.1%, beat 64%, recov 73%).
finding.where: backtest/surv.py lines 28-40 (MSH construction: NB_RET.get on bhavcopy epochs, -0.08 threshold on unadjusted closes) and lines 63-66 (w0 truncation + the 400-bar gate); same logic duplicated in final.py lines 44-47.

verdict.which_conclusion: none — (b) and (c) are strengthened, not moved; (a) was already retracted by the study itself (partly for this very mechanism) and the post-fix sign is the reverse of (a)
verdict.reasoning:
DEFECT IS REAL (not refuted), but the claim as filed misattributes its own mechanism, and nothing it touches moves a conclusion. The valuable output is that the SAME root cause is live in the current deliverable, in a place the claim does not name.

1. LIVE BUG — the headline portfolio table is still 100% survivorship-biased. `fixed_pf.py` builds PANEL from charting (epoch mod 86400 = 0, midnight UTC) AND bhavcopy (mod 86400 = 66600, midnight IST), then the sim iterates `for day in dates` drawn from `nb_d` and fills via `PANEL[sym].get(day)`. Measured: 398 delisted candidate signals are offered on a fill day, 0 are fillable; charting 2,456/2,456 (100%). So RESULTS.md's "The portfolio sim runs on the combined panel, so the deepest-first fill really does buy DHFL and HDIL and really does take them to zero" is FALSE — it buys none of them. Re-keying the bhavcopy half by +19,800s makes 395/398 fillable and the NCLT zero-marks finally fire (6 'wiped' exits at 20 slots). nodiv arm, published vs repaired: 20 slots hold-to-recovery 8.16%/-2.10pp -> 5.32%/-4.95pp (MDD -38.7 -> -44.6); 10 slots 11.25%/+0.98pp -> 2.81%/-7.46pp (MDD -37.4 -> -51.2); DEEP-only 20 slots 6.75%/-3.52pp -> 5.04%/-5.23pp (MDD -39.2 -> -50.0); +36m stop 20 slots 9.82%/-0.45pp -> 4.81%/-5.46pp (MDD -51.6 -> -63.6); sanitised-dividend 20 slots 9.46%/-0.81pp -> 6.40%/-3.87pp. Direction certain, magnitude +/- a few pp (the delisted walk-forward is unadjusted bhavcopy, so an unmasked bonus mid-hold could print a fake drop; A13 found 1 post-entry split among 39 restored, and the sign is secured by the real wiped exits). The 511-episode table is NOT affected: `grep` confirms fixed.py/fixed_run.py touch nb_d only via `np.searchsorted`, which tolerates the offset. Episode table stands; portfolio table is wrong.

2. THE CLAIM'S CITED MECHANISM IS REAL BUT 1.6% ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE DEAD GUARD. Confirmed: surv.py:35 `NB_RET.get(int(d[i]),0.0)` hits 0 of 4,215 bhavcopy dates (charting 4,400/4,400); fixed map 4,211/4,215. Truncation->MIN_BARS reproduces exactly (surv 3,181/4,629 = 68.7%, charting 9,961/23,132 = 43.1%). But the epoch fix ALONE recovers only 51 of the 3,181 truncation-killed slots (1.6%); MSH days 1,493 -> 1,346. Removing the detector entirely recovers 2,856 (89.8%). So the 3,181 is limb 2 — the detector running on unadjusted closes — which surv.py's own docstring declares a BOUND and which RESULTS.md reports as the ca_mode sensitivity, not limb 1.

3. THE EPOCH FIX MOVES NO ROBUST STATISTIC. Pushed through final.py's published classification/scaling: episodes 266 -> 267; shallow medAnnEx +6.7% unchanged; DEEP medAnnEx +10.6% unchanged (also unchanged under splits_only); all-entry medAnnEx +7.4 -> +7.1. Only the arithmetic mean moves (DEEP +41.4 -> +34.6), and the entire move is the 2 added episodes, both DUPLICATE monthly re-qualifications of symbols already counted — RELINFRA 2011-01-31 (-450% arith excess, 14.3y open) and ABAN 2016-05-31 (-314%, 9.3y open) — with RELINFRA 2011-02-28 dropping out. That is the unbounded-arithmetic-excess artifact plus the persistent-loser double-counting that RESULTS.md explicitly retracts.

4. (a) WAS NEVER SUPPORTED, SO NO DEFECT CAN MOVE IT. Bootstrap of the deep-minus-shallow medAnnEx gap: as-shipped +4.0pp [-5.4,+23.2], epoch-fixed +3.9pp [-5.5,+22.9], splits-only +3.4pp [-5.7,+22.7] — CI straddles zero under every arm, and shallow medAnnEx is positive (+6.7%/yr, beat 62%) under every arm, so "edge ONLY in deep" is false as shipped. RESULTS.md has since formally retracted it ("Deep-only is now the worst arm (-3.52pp), not the best"), citing this exact mechanism ("the same filter ran on the bhavcopy leg and deleted the real failures before they could be classified ... Survivorship leg 35 -> 49"), and marks surv.py/report.py/variants.py/final.py/merge2.py SUPERSEDED, "do not quote their output".

5. SEVERITY: "fatal" rejected. The bias runs uniformly IN FAVOUR of the rule, and all three conclusions are anti-rule, so none can flip — (b) is strengthened (the only index-beating arm, 10-slot +0.98pp, becomes -7.46pp), (c) is strengthened (true MDD -42% to -64%, never better than the index's -36.34%), (a) is pushed further in the direction already retracted. Material to the published figures (2.8-8.4pp on every portfolio row) and it falsifies one factual sentence in RESULTS.md, but the verdict never changes.

Also worth recording: surv.py's docstring calls that leg "a BOUND, not a precise measurement" — truncation makes it an UNDER-correction, so the bound points the wrong way. A framing error that strengthens (b)/(c) and moves nothing.

finding.title: The portfolio simulation is 100% uncorrected for survivorship, and its deepest-first ranking concentrates it in exactly the names it cannot see
finding.claim: portfolio() in report.py and pf() in variants.py build their price lookup as pxc={s:... for s in S}, i.e. only from the 338 charting symbols. The 112 charting-absent universe members - 17.1% of all universe slots and 36.6% of 2011 slots - can never be filled, so no portfolio run ever holds RCOM, SINTEX, RELCAPITAL, HDIL, DHFL, EDUCOMP, OPTOCIRCUI, IBREALEST (or TATAMOTORS and HDFC on the winning side). Worse, both sims sort candidates by -up (deepest discount first), which is precisely the ordering that fills the deepest-fallen names first - and the deepest-fallen are disproportionately the absentees. So the deepest-first ranking that produces the headline '+12.04pp' is the ranking that maximises exposure to the invisible set. RESULTS.md acknowledges the bias for the episode table ('the bias that is NOT yet in those numbers') and then presents the portfolio table with no correction at all, while calling the portfolio sim 'the behavioural truth'.
finding.direction: In favour of the rule. All portfolio CAGRs and Calmars are biased up and the max drawdowns biased toward zero.
finding.magnitude: Making the 112 absentees fillable from bhavcopy. LOWER BOUND, using the study's own (broken) detector so only the 204 candidate slots it would itself have found: 10-slot 36-month stop 22.31% CAGR / +12.04pp -> 18.68% / +8.41pp; 20-slot 36m +4.37pp -> +3.17pp; 20-slot hold-to-recovery -1.10pp -> -2.19pp. With the detector fixed: 10-slot 36m -> 6.74% CAGR, MDD -27.66% -> -62.23%, Calmar 0.81 -> 0.11, +12.04pp -> -3.53pp; 20-slot 36m 14.64% -> 12.37% (+2.10pp); 20-slot hold-to-recovery 9.16% -> 8.36% (-1.91pp); 10-slot hold-to-recovery 11.48% -> 8.30% (+1.21pp -> -1.97pp). Terminal-mark treatment is almost irrelevant (no-haircut variant 7.28% vs 6.74%), so the damage is the price path, not the recovery assumption. Realised wipeouts appear only in the full-universe runs: EDUCOMP -100%, HDIL -100%, DHFL -100%, SINTEX -99%, RELCAPITAL -97%, RCOM -80%.
finding.empirical: audit/a10.py A21 (shipped vs full-universe portfolio grid, 10/20 slots x hold-to-recovery/36m) and A22 (lower bound on the study's own detector; generous no-haircut variant). Shipped baselines reproduced exactly from variants.log/main.log (11.48/9.16/22.31/14.64%).
finding.where: backtest/report.py line 88 (pxc built from S only) and variants.py line 48 (same), with the deepest-first fill at report.py line 81 / variants.py line 42 (sort key -up).
finding.short_summary: Portfolio sim can only ever hold the 338 survivors

verdict.which_conclusion: none
verdict.reasoning:
DEFECT CONFIRMED, severity "fatal" justified for the portfolio table, but it moves none of (a)/(b)/(c) — it pushes all three further in the direction the study already took.

CODE FACT, verified. report.py:88 and variants.py:48 build `pxc` from `S`, the charting panel (338 symbols). Every shipped portfolio cell logs "absentee fills 0" when instrumented. The claim's arithmetic is exact: 112 of 450 universe symbols absent (24.9%), 4,768 of 27,900 universe slots (17.1%), 659 of 1,800 2011 slots (36.6%). 33 of the 112 do generate qualifying signals — 652 monthly signals against the charting leg's 1,146, so roughly a third of all signals were structurally invisible. The deepest-first mechanism is real too: on 94 of the 95 dates carrying an absentee signal, at least one absentee ranks inside the merged top-10 by -up.

MAGNITUDE. Snapping the bhavcopy panel onto the charting calendar (its epochs are 18:30 UTC vs 00:00 UTC — 0% exact match, so a naive merge would have measured zero delta), split-adjusting from miss_splits.json, and forcing a terminal exit when a series dies: the 10-slot/36-month headline falls from 22.31% CAGR (+12.04pp) to 7.68% (generous, no haircut on any delisting = A22 lower bound) or 7.03% (classified). MDD −27.66% → −61.95%; Calmar 0.81 → 0.12. A control arm (charting only + the same forced-terminal rule) reproduces all six shipped cells to 0.01pp, so the whole delta is the universe fix, not my terminal rule. Direction is as claimed: CAGRs and Calmars biased up, drawdowns biased toward zero. At the 2020-03-24 trough the full-universe 10-slot book held 5 absentees (RELCAPITAL −99.3%, IBREALEST −77.4%, UJJIVAN −63.1%, INFRATEL −59.1%, DHFL −51.9%); the shipped book held none. Ranking the same absentees LAST instead of by -up recovers 7.68% → 12.85%, so ~5.2pp of the damage is specifically the deepest-first ordering the claim names.

GENERATOR PARITY, the one objection that could have cut the other way, resolved against the study. The study's own absentee generator (final.MC, 204 signals, 16 symbols) admits zero symbols mine does not and censors 17 that mine admits — ARSSINFRA, DHFL, EDUCOMP, HDIL, IBREALEST, IBULHSGFIN, INFRATEL, JPASSOCIAT, OPTOCIRCUI, UJJIVAN and others, i.e. nearly every real failure. That is the circular bug fixed.py already documented (the ≥8% crash detector deletes NCLT-bound names). So the "parity" arm (22.31 → 18.69) excludes the losers by construction and is not a floor. With both legs on clean generators the charting-only baseline is 16.52% and the full universe gives 5.42% (−4.85pp), MDD −65.17%. Across every arm whose absentee leg is uncensored, the corrected 36m/10 lands at 5–8% against NIFTYBEES's 10.27%.

WHY IT MOVES NOTHING.
(b) "held-to-recovery does not beat NIFTYBEES" is CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED. The one shipped cell that beat the index (10-slot h2r, +1.21pp) trails in every corrected arm: 6.19–8.41% vs 10.27%. Nothing to move.
(c) "not safe alpha for real money" is STRENGTHENED without exception — every CAGR falls, every Calmar falls, every MDD worsens. A bias that pushes returns down cannot make the rule look safe.
(a) "edge only in deep ≤−35% entries" is NOT MOVED. Running the explicit buckets through the full-universe sim at 10 slots/36m: deep +11.07pp → +5.33pp, shallow +1.96pp → −3.44pp. The spread is 9.1pp before and 8.8pp after; at 20 slots 3.6pp → 2.7pp. Both arms drop ~5pp together, so the relative statement survives (and sharpens: shallow goes from roughly flat to negative). What IS destroyed is the proxy RESULTS.md used for it — "10 slots ≈ the deep bucket, hence +12.04pp". Concentration inverts: shipped 10 slots beat 20 (22.31 v 14.64), corrected 10 slots lose to 20 (7.68 v 12.89).

WHAT STILL NEEDS FIXING even though no conclusion moves: the portfolio table's +12.04pp and +4.37pp are both unsupportable, so RESULTS.md headline #2 ("a 2–3 year time stop is what makes it work at all") must be restated, and calling the portfolio sim "the behavioural truth" while the ⚠️ section below it says the bias "is NOT yet in those numbers" is backwards — the sim is the leg MOST exposed to the bias, because the fill order targets the invisible names. Caveats on my own numbers, none of which flip a boolean: TATAMOTORS and TATAMTRDVR take two of twenty slots for one company; the hard-split sensitivity is non-monotone (cutting a series frees a slot) so it is not a strict floor; 4 of the 33 absentee signal symbols lack fmp dividend rows.

finding.title: 53 symbols and 907 universe slots clear the -25%-off-high trigger and are then silently dropped because fmp.income_statement has no FY rows for them
finding.claim: mlatest_fy() returns (None, None) when FMP carries no FY income statement for a symbol, and the caller does a bare `continue`. On the charting leg this gate costs 1 slot of 23,132 (0.004%). On the missing-name leg it costs 216 slots / 22 symbols under the shipped detector, and 907 slots / 53 symbols once the detector stops killing them earlier at MIN_BARS. 51 of the 53 have exactly ZERO FY rows with an EPS. The list is the Indian insolvency roll: IVRCLINFRA, LITL (Lanco Infratech), AMTEKAUTO, BHUSANSTL, ALOKTEXT, GITANJALI, KFA (Kingfisher), ABGSHIP, ORCHIDCHEM, PIPAVAVYD, FRL (Future Retail), EVERONN, SATYAMCOMP, FINANTECH (NSEL), HANUNG, ISPATIND - plus the bank amalgamations (ORIENTBANK 75 slots, ALBK 55, DENABANK 41, ANDHRABANK, SYNDIBANK, VIJAYABANK, IDFCBANK) which the study would drop anyway. So fmp.income_statement is itself a survivor-biased panel for India, and the survivorship correction inherits that bias at the gate it cannot evaluate. These episodes are unmeasured, not bounded: the 'BOUND: every unverified ticker treated as a TOTAL LOSS' arm in merge2.py cannot reach them because they never become candidates.
finding.direction: In favour of the rule. The uncovered names are dead companies, so excluding them removes failures only.
finding.magnitude: Estimated 20-45 additional failure episodes - 2-3x the 13 the study folded in - from 907 trigger-passing slots x the visible leg's 35.6% pass rate through the fundamentals gates (1,146 of 3,219 slots that reach them) / 6.9 candidate slots per episode on the survivorship leg. Roughly half the 53 are amalgamations the study would drop, so call it 10-25 net kept failures. Not folded into my restated numbers above, so every deep-bucket figure I quote is still an upper bound.

verdict.reasoning:
The defect is REAL and code-confirmed, but its stated composition is wrong and its "material" severity does not survive measurement.

CONFIRMED IN CODE. surv.py:47-51 `av=[x for x in MFU.get(s,[]) if x[1]<=t]; if not av: return None,None`, consumed at surv.py:72 and final.py:53 as `if now is None or now[4] is None or now[4]<=0: continue`. WHERE IT BREAKS — MAGNITUDE. Forcing every blocked slot to PASS gates 6-11 (the hard ceiling the study lacks) gives, as the code actually ships, 50 episodes of which only 4 are genuine-loss names; folding those in at net = -100% moves DEEP mean excess +41.4%→+33.9% and median +26.3%→+23.0%, leaving deep-minus-shallow at +58.6pp mean / +12.7pp median. Scaling the measured 18-30% pass rate and ~0.12-0.18 episodes/slot onto the 198 genuinely-absent loss slots gives ~7 episodes and ~3 deep, against a threshold of 10.

finding.claim: merge2.py's docstring defends dropping RENAME/MERGER_SHARE_SWAP/DEMERGER by citing net returns ('TATAMOTORS +36.6%, HDFC +21.4%, SRTRANSFIN +38.9%, CADILAHC +58.7%'). So the drop removes losers from the shallow bucket, which flatters it. Second issue: the drop is applied per symbol, not per episode. 14 of the 22 dropped episodes are CLOSED - the stock regained its frozen 2-year high and the position exited YEARS before the rename (CADILAHC x3, CENTURYTEX x2, SRTRANSFIN x3, TATAMOTORS x2, TATAMTRDVR x3, AMARAJABAT). Those are fully measured, unambiguous outcomes thrown away. Third: the successors are all in the charting panel (HDFCBANK, LTIM, SHRIRAMFIN, ZYDUSLIFE, TATACONSUM, CGPOWER, IDFCFIRSTB), so the true holder path through a rename was measurable and simply was not measured - most consequentially TATAMOTORS, absent for 181 of 186 universe months, whose 2018-2020 de-rating and recovery is the decade's largest instance of the pattern under test.
finding.direction: Against the rule on the shallow bucket (the shipped -23.5% is too harsh), in favour on the deep bucket. Net direction on claim (b) is against the rule, i.e. the write-up's conservatism claim is wrong in sign but happens to support its own conclusion.

finding.empirical: audit/a1.py A1 (all 35 raw survivorship episodes with bucket, classification, net, excess and open flag; the 2x2 bucket-by-action table giving shallow DROP meanExc -92.5% / deep DROP +29.4%) and A2 (base 253 = 205 shallow + 48 deep; kept_verified 13 = 7 shallow + 6 deep); a5.py A10 (the 'BOUND: base + every restored episode at its raw bhavcopy mark' row, n=338).

finding.short_summary: Rename drop defended in net, headline is excess; 14 drops already closed

verdict.reasoning:
REAL on its two mechanical points, but its stated direction is backwards and its third argument is factually wrong.

**(1) Per-symbol drop discards per-episode closed outcomes — CONFIRMED.** merge2.py line 45 (`if cl in DROP: drops[cl]+=1; continue`) has no `x['open']` test, and the classification is keyed on symbol (line 38, `agent_cls[s]`). So 22 episodes are dropped, of which **14 are CLOSED** — they hit the frozen 2-year high and exited 1.5-10 years BEFORE the corporate event cited to justify the drop: SRTRANSFIN exits 2014-05-15/18 vs the Nov-2022 SHRIRAMFIN rename; CENTURYTEX exits 2014-06-30 vs the 2024 ABREL rename; CADILAHC exits 2020-10/2020-12/2021-04 vs Feb-2022 Zydus; TATAMTRDVR exits 2023-07-25 vs the Sep-2024 DVR conversion; TATAMOTORS exits 2023-07-06 vs the Oct-2025 demerger; AMARAJABAT exits 2020-11-26 vs 2023-04. The drop's rationale ("holder made whole via a successor we do not have") cannot apply to a position already closed at target. 14 fully-measured, unambiguous outcomes are thrown away. The 8 OPEN dropped episodes (HDFC x2, IDFC x2, L&TFH, LTI, AMARAJABAT 2021, CADILAHC 2021) are correctly dropped.

**(2) The conservatism defence is stated in the wrong metric — CONFIRMED.** merge2.py line 6 and RESULTS.md ("Renames and swaps are dropped, which is conservative — they showed as winners (TATAMOTORS +36.6%, SRTRANSFIN +38.9%, CADILAHC +58.7%, HDFC +21.4%)") argue in NET returns; the table those words defend reports mean EXCESS. Under excess, dropping the shallow episodes RAISED the shallow number. A1's 2x2 reproduces (shallow DROP meanExc -92.5%, deep DROP +29.4%).

**But the claimed DIRECTION is wrong in sign on BOTH buckets.** Measured by restoring the dropped episodes at raw bhavcopy marks (r1.py):
- shallow mean arithmetic excess: **-23.5% shipped → -24.8%** (+14 closed) **→ -28.1%** (all 22). The shipped -23.5% was too KIND, not "too harsh" as the claim asserts.
- deep median annualised excess: **+10.6% → +15.4%/yr**; deep mean arith excess +41.4% → +42.9%. The shipped deep was too harsh, not "in favour". Only the all-22 arith mean (+40.0%) nudges the claim's way, and that is driven by the 2 open episodes where the drop is correct.
- deep-minus-shallow gap on **median annualised excess** — the metric RESULTS.md actually stands behind, having already retracted arithmetic excess as an artefact (lines 106-135, "Both numbers are artifacts and that conclusion does not stand"): **+3.97pp shipped → +8.95pp → +6.81pp.** Fixing the defect WIDENS the deep/shallow split. Shallow median annEx stays positive (+6.4%/+5.8%/yr), so the doc's corrected "shallow is not value-destroying" also survives.

**(3) Claim's third argument fails on two counts.** "The successors are all in the charting panel" is false: 5 of the 10 dropped symbols' successors are absent from `S` (AMARAJABAT→ARE&M, CENTURYTEX→ABREL, LTI→LTIM, TATAMOTORS→TMPV, TATAMTRDVR→TATAMOTORS-new). Two of the seven tickers it names — TATACONSUM and CGPOWER — are successors of nothing in the DROP set. And the "most consequential" case is wrong: **TATAMOTORS 2018-2020 was never enterable.** It is in the universe and 25-81% off its 2-year high at every decision date 2017-06 → 2020-10, but fails the rule's EPS leg at every one: EPS growth -29% / -33% / -56% (FY2016/17/18), then outright losses (NI -₹28,826 cr FY2019, -₹12,071 cr FY2020, -₹13,451 cr FY2021). A filter exclusion, not a measurement gap — it is not an instance of the pattern under test.

Also: IDFC -436.6%, the claim's largest cited "loser removed", is itself an unadjusted-bhavcopy artefact (r3.py). Its frozen highs (218.25, 185.30) are pre-demerger; after the 2015 IDFC Bank spin-off the unadjusted series never closes above 130.70, so both episodes are structurally unexitable and stay open to the 2024 merger, accruing arithmetic excess purely because the index compounded 9-13 years against a stub. That is exactly the contamination the DROP was built to exclude.

**Does it move (a), (b) or (c)? No — every restoration moves every bucket in the direction that REINFORCES the shipped conclusions.**
- (a) edge only in deep ≤-35%: strengthened (gap +3.97 → +8.95pp median annEx).
- (b) held-to-recovery does not beat NIFTYBEES: **unreachable by construction.** `portfolio()` (report.py:75) and `pf()` (variants.py:38) consume `candidates(**BASE)`, which iterates the charting panel `S`; `MS` and `surv_episodes` appear nowhere in study.py / report.py / variants.py / main.py. The 9.16% vs 10.27% CAGR headline cannot be touched by merge2.py's DROP. On the episode metric the all-entry mean excess goes -10.3% → -10.5% → -13.6%, slightly more adverse.
- (c) not safe alpha: reinforced. The deep bucket's +4.8pp/yr bump rests on 5 restored episodes of 3 symbols inside a 59-episode bucket over 15.7 years, in the per-episode-ratio aggregation the doc itself says not to quote.

Severity: real, **below "material"** by the task's definition. Minor conservatism note: the restored marks carry `divd=0.0` (surv.py:98) where `walk2` adds `DV`, so the restorations are slightly understated — does not change sign.

**Recommended fix (not applied — I am the refutation subagent):** (i) merge2.py line 45 → `if cl in DROP and x['open']: drops[cl]+=1; continue`, which restores the 14 closed episodes and correctly keeps the 8 open ones dropped; (ii) rewrite merge2.py line 6 and the RESULTS.md "which is conservative — they showed as winners" sentence — it is false under the table's own metric regardless of materiality, and it currently reads as a sign-correct defence when the sign is wrong.

Scope note: the auditor's cited a5.py A10 "BOUND, n=338" row is built from `leg_splits_only.json` (85 episodes, a different detector) — a sibling audit item, not merge2.py's defect. merge2.py processes the 35-episode leg; that is what was measured here.

finding.title: Excess return is never horizon-normalised, and every survivorship correction is an open-ended position, so the correction's magnitude is a horizon artefact
finding.claim: walk()/surv_episodes() compute excess as net minus the benchmark's total return over the identical calendar window, with no annualisation and no cap on the window. Holding periods in the corrected sample span 38 to 5,729 days. Because a survivorship failure by definition never reaches its target, every kept failure is 'open' and is marked at the last bar, so each one draws the maximum-length benchmark leg: RELINFRA 2011-02-28 to 2025-06-03 is 5,209 days, net -38.7% against a benchmark of +394.5%, giving an 'excess' of -433.1%; BGRENERGY -424.5% over 5,442 days; five SINTEX episodes between -219% and -236%. 46 of the 266 corrected episodes have |excess| > 100% and they account for 209% of the sum of all excesses. So both the deep bucket's +41.4% (driven up by a handful of multi-year compounders) and the size of the survivorship haircut (driven down by six maximal-horizon failures) are artefacts of mixing 6-month and 15-year holds in one arithmetic mean. The write-up half-sees this ('the mean/median split is the whole story') but still states claim (a) in means.
finding.direction: Unclear in sign; it amplifies the magnitude of every mean-excess number in both directions and makes the deep-vs-shallow comparison non-comparable, since deep entries take a median 27.7 months versus 20.1 for shallow.
finding.magnitude: Mechanically large. The 13 kept failures move the deep bucket by -28.5pp (+69.9% -> +41.4%) and the shallow bucket by only -4.5pp (-19.0% -> -23.5%), and that asymmetry is driven by holding-period length rather than by severity. A per-trade annualised or horizon-matched excess would shrink the spread between the buckets; report.py already computes a per-trade annualised figure and the mean there is +128.6% (+561,836.6% on the overlapping-signal sample), which shows the metric is unusable as written.
finding.empirical: audit/a5.py A11 (per-episode entry/exit/days/net/bench/excess for all 13 kept failures; holding-period spread 38-5,729 days; 46/266 episodes with |excess|>100% contributing 209% of the excess sum); derived bucket decomposition base deep +69.9% -> +41.4% from a5.py A10.
finding.where: backtest/study.py lines 167-173 (walk bench/excess) and surv.py lines 95-99; aggregated in report.py hit_table lines 36-44 and merge2.py/final.py table().

verdict.reasoning:
NOT REFUTED as a mechanic — every number reproduces exactly — but NOT MATERIAL, because the study's own write-up already contains this correction and the three conclusions do not rest on the broken metric.

CONFIRMED IN CODE: study.py:166-173, surv.py:95-99, variants.py:31-36 and final.py:28-33 all compute `bench = nb_c[bj]/nb_c[bi]-1` over the trade's exact calendar window and `excess = net - bench`, with no annualisation and no cap on window length. report.py:36-44 and merge2.py/final.py `table()` aggregate that into arithmetic means.

CONFIRMED IN DATA (all exact): holding periods span 38..5,729 days (median 639); 46/266 corrected episodes have |excess| > 100%, summing -57.410 against an all-episode sum of -27.467 = 209%; RELINFRA 5,209d net -38.68% / bench +394.45% / excess -433.13%; BGRENERGY 5,442d -424.5%; five SINTEX episodes -219.1/-223.5/-228.7/-231.9/-236.0%; DEEP bucket mean excess base +70.1% -> corrected +41.4% (claim said +69.9%, a 0.2pp difference). The claim is also right that the survivorship haircut is a mean artefact: all-entries mean excess moves -2.0% -> -10.3% (-8.3pp) while median excess moves only +14.0% -> +12.2% (-1.8pp) and median net -0.3pp.

THREE SUB-CLAIMS ARE EMPIRICALLY FALSE:
1. "every kept failure is 'open' and is marked at the last bar, so each one draws the maximum-length benchmark leg" — 4 of the 13 kept failures are CLOSED: RELCAPITAL recovered to target at 945d (+46.1%), 853d (+34.5%) and 351d (+56.2%), ABAN at 291d (+147.1%). Kept-failure days range 291..5,442, not uniformly maximal.
2. "The write-up ... still states claim (a) in means" — FALSE for the current RESULTS.md. It carries a dedicated section, "Why per-trade excess is the wrong metric here (a correction to my own first pass)", that names this exact mechanism ("RELINFRA, held 14.3 years, scores -433% excess simply because the index compounded 4.6x meanwhile"), states "Both numbers are artifacts and that conclusion does not stand", reports the HINDPETRO concentration (161% of the deep bucket's excess from three episodes of one stock), gives trimmed-mean (+41.4% -> +2.1%) and median-annualised tables, and stamps the mean-excess column "the metric criticised in the warning section; the bucket split it implies is not reliable." A header warning also tells the reader not to quote any per-trade excess figure. The orchestrator's (a) traces to a pre-correction state.
3. "makes the deep-vs-shallow comparison non-comparable" — the comparison survives horizon normalisation: on annualised excess (trade CAGR - index CAGR, same window) deep is +10.6%/yr vs shallow +6.7%/yr, and in horizon-matched day bins deep leads shallow in all four (bins are thin, n_deep 14/11/10/19, so this is directional not decisive).

CONCLUSION MOVEMENT — none of the three move:
(b) is immune by construction. `portfolio()` (report.py:121-128) and `pf()` (variants.py:91) derive CAGR from the compounded equity curve and b_cagr from the raw NIFTYBEES series; `excess` is produced only by walk/walk2/mwalk2 for the event-study tables and never enters the portfolio path. The headline 20-slot 9.16% vs NIFTYBEES 10.27% (-1.10pp) stands untouched, and RESULTS.md already designates it "the one headline number that is capital-weighted rather than an average of ratios, so it is the one to trust."
(c) rests on (b) plus MDD never beating the index (-27.7% to -38.0% vs -36.34%), 54 deep episodes over 15.7y, 60-130 closed portfolio trades, 10-slot 22.31% vs 20-slot 14.64% concentration sensitivity, and 2008 being untestable. (a) is not a conclusion of the current write-up at all — it is the author's retracted first-pass reading, and this metric problem is the documented reason it was retracted. audit.lens: corpactions — corporate-action handling (the level-shift detector, `ca_mode`, and the CA treatment inside the survivorship merge)

findings.title: The level-shift detector is 96.4% false positives: it is an earnings-crash detector, not a corporate-action detector
findings.claim: RESULTS.md concedes the 2,722 flags are "too many for genuine corporate actions" but never measures it. Of the 2,722 flags, only 70 (2.6%) fall within ±5 days of any split/bonus ex-date in the study's own `fmp.splits_calendar` pull, and 27 (1.0%) within ±3 days of a dividend worth ≥4% of price. 2,625 (96.4%) match nothing. 561 flags land on days the index fell 2–4% (inside the −4% guard) and 76 land on the 15 worst NIFTYBEES days, so a slice are plain beta, not even idiosyncratic. The worst-flagged symbols are PRAKASHSTL (47), ONELIFECAP (35), BEDMUTHA (32), UNITECH (31), SUZLON (28) — volatility, not corporate actions. The detector's stated purpose (unreachable targets from unadjusted CAs) has a measured effect of about 1pp on the recovery rate: 83% under `truncate`, 84% under `off` (no handling at all), 84% under a CA-only arm.
findings.direction: Against the rule's measured universe in a way that FAVOURS the rule's reported statistics: the flags select out high-volatility names, and because of finding #2 the selection is lethal rather than cosmetic.
findings.magnitude: 70 of 2,722 flags are genuine CAs. The stated benefit is ~1pp of recovery rate; the unintended cost is 54% of qualifying signals (finding #2).

findings.title: `ca_mode='truncate'` is not truncation — MIN_BARS=400 turns it into near-total exclusion, deleting 54% of qualifying signals
findings.claim: After truncation the code re-applies `if j-i0+1 < MIN_BARS: continue` (MIN_BARS=400) to the SHORTENED window. A full 2-year window holds ~496 bars, so any flag inside the most recent ~19 of the 24 months leaves <400 bars and the candidate is silently dropped rather than truncated. Measured over all 23,132 universe slots: 11,511 (50%) carry at least one flag in window; 10,183 of those (88%) are killed by MIN_BARS and only 1,328 keep a truncated window. Of the 253 headline episodes, just 7 (3%) were actually truncated. Signals: 2,478 with no CA handling, 2,416 under a CA-only arm, 1,146 under `truncate`, 1,055 under `exclude` — so `truncate` destroys 1,270 of the 2,416 signals a real CA correction would keep, and `truncate`'s surviving set is a strict subset of the CA-only set (0 signals exist only under `truncate`). This also makes the "253 vs 233" truncate/exclude sensitivity tautological: at 7 truncations the two arms are the same arm.
findings.direction: Unclear a priori, FAVOURABLE in fact — the deleted names are disproportionately deep and disproportionately catastrophic (findings #3 and #4).
findings.magnitude: 1,270 of 2,416 signals (53%) and 200 of 453 episodes (44%) deleted. 832 of the 1,270 deleted signals (65%) were deep (≤−35% off).

findings.title: The survivorship correction — "the decisive table" — deletes the real failures before they can be classified
findings.claim: The same detector+MIN_BARS mechanism runs on the bhavcopy leg. It kills 3,301 of the 3,567 flagged missing-name slots, cutting the survivorship leg from 85 episodes to 35. The correct counterfactual (keep surv.py:32's split dates, since bhavcopy IS unadjusted, and drop only the crash loop at :33-39) restores 27 episodes — including every one of DHFL, HDIL (×2), EDUCOMP, ARSSINFRA and OPTOCIRCUI. All six are DEEP (≤−35% off) and all six are catastrophic: net −65.8%, −96.7%, −96.9%, −98.1%, −92.1%, −82.5%. This is circular by construction: a company that goes to NCLT necessarily has ≥8% down days, so the CA filter removes exactly the names the survivorship correction exists to capture. RESULTS.md names HDIL and IBREALEST as "exactly the names that matter" and then reports a correction that contains neither — the classification fan-out was never shown them. Neither DHFL, HDIL nor ARSSINFRA has a split during its hold, and the in-window splits (EDUCOMP 2009-10-27, OPTOCIRCUI 2012-03-29) are correctly truncated in the split-only arm, so these are not CA artefacts.

findings.title: The 54-episode deep bucket is a detector artefact — the honest count is 113–119, and the detector removes deep episodes at a higher rate than shallow
findings.claim: Conclusion (c) rests on "54 favourable episodes in 15.7 years (~3.4/year)". The removal is selective: the detector drops 59 of 107 deep episodes (55%) but 141 of 346 shallow (41%), because a stock that is ≥35% off its 2-year high almost always got there via at least one ≥8% down day. Among passing signals the depth reading is also wrong — on the 6,838 slots where a false-positive flag lowered the high, measured "% off the high" is pulled UP by a median 18.9pp (p90 48.3pp) — but the damage is overwhelmingly deletion, not mis-measurement: only 2 passing signals change bucket.

findings.claim: Testing the specific claim (a): removing the detector's false positives moves the deep bucket from +41.4% to +25.4% mean excess and the shallow band from −23.5% to −10.5%; adding the 6 deleted survivorship failures takes the deep bucket to +13.8% (CA-only) or +16.7% (base arm). findings.title: The sensitivity arm offered as proof that CA handling is immaterial never tests the claim it is cited for
findings.claim: RESULTS.md asserts "Corporate-action handling does not drive the result" and "Sensitivity arms show it does not drive the result", citing exclude/off at 233/459 episodes with median excess +15.4%/+19.0%. That row reports MEDIAN excess for ALL entries. The headline conclusion is a MEAN-excess split BY off-high bucket, and that split was never computed under any CA arm other than `truncate` — final.py imports `C` from variants.py, which is hard-wired to `ca_mode='truncate'`.
