audit.verdict_on_conclusion:
This lens challenges the quoted numbers behind ALL THREE conclusions, and challenges (a) and (c) as arguments.

(a) "the edge lives ENTIRELY in deep entries, +41.4% vs −23.5%" — DOES NOT SURVIVE. The deep-bucket edge does survive a clean corporate-actions-only correction in sign (+25.4% mean excess at n=113), so the answer to the brief's question "does the deep edge survive ca_mode='off'?" is yes — it is +40.1% at n=116 under `off` and +37.4% at n=107 under the clean CA-only arm, and the `off` arm is NOT materially contaminated by raw splits (only 12 of 459 episodes carry one; removing them moves mean excess by 0.4pp). But both quoted magnitudes are inflated by the CA code in opposite directions, and once the 6 real-failure survivorship episodes the CA filter deleted before classification are restored, deep mean excess is +13.8% (CA-only) to +16.7% (base), and on median annualised excess the deep/shallow ordering inverts in the base arm (+4.5%/yr deep vs +6.3%/yr shallow). The shallow band's "they destroy value, −23.5%" is −10.5% once false-positive exclusions are restored. A separate lens already retracted (a) on tail concentration; this lens reaches the same verdict independently via selection, and adds that the shallow band was never value-destroying.

(b) "held to recovery it does NOT beat NIFTYBEES: 20-slot 9.16% vs 10.27%" — the specific number is a detector artefact and flips sign to 10.83% vs 10.27% (+0.56pp) under the clean arm, so the write-up's "one headline number to trust" is not trustworthy as stated. Treat +0.56pp as an upper bound, not a rehabilitation: portfolio() runs on the charting panel only, so no portfolio arm holds a single survivorship name, and the deepest-first fill would have bought DHFL and HDIL. The conclusion "does not meaningfully beat the index" therefore stands; the number supporting it does not. More damaging to the write-up as it now reads: its new lead finding, the 36-month-stop rescue (10 slots, 22.31% CAGR, MDD −27.66%, Calmar 0.81), collapses to 16.45% / −54.47% / 0.30 under the clean arm — far worse drawdown than the index, not better.

(c) "not a safe alpha: 54 favourable episodes in 15.7 years, drawdown no better than the index" — the SAMPLE-SIZE half of this argument is a detector artefact and should be withdrawn: the honest deep count is 113–119, i.e. 7.6/year not 3.4/year. The CONCLUSION nonetheless survives and strengthens, for different reasons: deep mean excess is ~+14-17% not +41%, the deep bucket is tail-driven under every CA arm (top-3 episodes = 107% of total deep excess; drop them and the mean is negative), every restored failure is a deep near-total loss, and the clean-arm time-stop drawdown is −54%, i.e. materially WORSE than the index rather than merely no better. Do not approve. The whole CA layer needs rebuilding before any number in RESULTS.md is quotable: replace the crash detector with the ca_audit RAW/AMBIG split list plus an explicit demerger list, decouple MIN_BARS from the truncated window (require 400 bars of the FULL window, not the truncated one, or truncate without re-testing), and on the bhavcopy leg keep split dates and drop the detector entirely — then re-run the classification fan-out over the 27 survivorship episodes it has never seen.

finding.title: `ca_mode='truncate'` is not truncation — MIN_BARS=400 turns it into near-total exclusion, deleting 54% of qualifying signals

Signals off 2,478 / truncate 1,146 / exclude 1,055. Episodes off 459 / truncate 253 / exclude 233. All match.

TWO SUB-NUMBERS IN THE CLAIM ARE WRONG, both inherited from a mislabel in the auditor's own run.log:
1. "just 7 (3%) of the 253 episodes were actually truncated" — no: 38 of 253 (15%) ran a truncated window, and 91 of 1,146 signals did. The auditor's 7 is `HI_OFF > hi*1.001`, i.e. episodes whose TARGET was lowered, printed under the label "window WAS truncated".
2. "truncate's surviving set is a strict subset... 0 signals exist only under truncate" and "the two arms are the same arm" — against the maximal `off` arm, 7 signals exist ONLY under truncate (truncation pulled pe_need back under the 35x cap). And truncate strictly contains exclude: exclude\truncate = 0, truncate\exclude = 91 signals → 20 extra episodes. The "253 vs 233" row is therefore not literally tautological; it measures a real 91-signal difference. The structural point survives though: the arm labelled "truncate" is just "exclude" plus 8% of the flagged population, so it spans almost none of the dimension it claims to probe.

DIRECTION is split, not "FAVOURABLE". The killed set IS disproportionately deep (896/1,339 = 67% deep vs 534/1,146 = 47% among kept), confirming the claim's finding #3. But the killed names' forward outcomes are GOOD, not catastrophic: medNet +65.3%, meanNet +83.1%, medExc +23.4%, meanExc +10.1%, p10Net −19.9%. So restoring them RAISES the deep median excess (+26.3% → +35.5%) and LOWERS the deep mean (+41.4% → +28.8%). Favourable on means, unfavourable on medians.

SEVERITY: not fatal. This is a real reporting/robustness defect — it silently deletes 88% of the flagged population and makes a labelled CA sensitivity nearly vacuous — but the study's decision-relevant bottom line survives and gets stronger. Note also that dropping a slot with <400 comparable bars is a defensible conservative choice, not obviously a bug: a 3-month window labelled "2-year high" would be worse (truncated targets understate the true high by median +14.9%, p90 +70.9%). The right fix is naming and reporting — stop calling the arm "truncate", drop the 253-vs-233 row as a CA sensitivity — plus fixing the detector's separate 96.4% false-positive rate, not lowering MIN_BARS.

finding.title: The survivorship correction — "the decisive table" — deletes the real failures before they can be classified
finding.claim: The same detector+MIN_BARS mechanism runs on the bhavcopy leg. It kills 3,301 of the 3,567 flagged missing-name slots, cutting the survivorship leg from 85 episodes to 35. All six are DEEP (≤−35% off) and all six are catastrophic: net −65.8%, −96.7%, −96.9%, −98.1%, −92.1%, −82.5%. This is circular by construction: a company that goes to NCLT necessarily has ≥8% down days, so the CA filter removes exactly the names the survivorship correction exists to capture. RESULTS.md names HDIL and IBREALEST as "exactly the names that matter" and then reports a correction that contains neither — the classification fan-out was never shown them. Neither DHFL, HDIL nor ARSSINFRA has a split during its hold, and the in-window splits (EDUCOMP 2009-10-27, OPTOCIRCUI 2012-03-29) are correctly truncated in the split-only arm, so these are not CA artefacts.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, and it is worse than claimed — the defect has three layers, not one.

LAYER 1 — mechanism is in the code at the cited lines. surv.py:32 builds the shift set from split dates; :33-39 adds a >=8% single-day-drop detector (skipped only if NIFTY itself fell >=4% and the price did not bounce half-way back within 5 bars); :64 truncates the 2-year-high window to the LAST shift; :66 then requires 400 bars. final.py:44-47 duplicates it when building MC. A name collapsing toward NCLT necessarily prints >=8% idiosyncratic down days, so the filter removes exactly the names the correction exists to capture. Circular by construction, as claimed.

LAYER 2 — magnitudes reproduce exactly (my v1.py, independent of the auditor's run3/run5). 4,629 missing-name universe slots have a bar; 3,567 carry a flag in window; 3,301 are KILLED by MIN_BARS, 266 survive truncated. Shipped MSH = 1,493 flags vs 167 split-only. surv_episodes(): shipped 35, split-only 85, MSH-off 88. The 27 deleted episodes span 15 symbols. All six claimed catastrophes verified to the decimal — DHFL off -92.9% net -65.8%, HDIL -73.6%/-96.7% and -39.9%/-96.9%, EDUCOMP -54.4%/-98.1%, ARSSINFRA -76.4%/-92.1%, OPTOCIRCUI -89.3%/-82.5% — all off<=-0.35, all open, all delisted(). The "not CA artefacts" leg holds: no split in any hold; DHFL/HDIL/ARSSINFRA/OPTOCIRCUI's in-window flags are all detector flags (DHFL 18, OPTOCIRCUI 14); EDUCOMP's 2009-10-27 and OPTOCIRCUI's 2012-03-29 splits ARE kept and correctly truncated in the split-only arm, and both episodes still qualify.

LAYER 3 — which the claim only gestures at, and which I demonstrated. classifications_partial.json (10 symbols) + final.py FALLBACK (6) = exactly the 16 symbols the BUGGY arm emits. So final.py:71 (`cl is None -> continue`) silently drops all 15 restored symbols even after MSH is fixed: fixing the detector alone changes the table for the already-classified names only. Separately, the fix adds 10 episodes to the SIX names RESULTS.md says it did fold in — bhavcopy episodes kept goes 13 -> 23 (ABAN 1->4, RELCAPITAL 3->5, RELINFRA 2->4, SINTEX 5->8), including ABAN -93.3% and -92.2%, RCOM -97.8%, RELCAPITAL -97.5%, SINTEX -87.5% and -70.5%, none with a split in its hold. So "Only 6 symbols are real failures ... = 13 episodes" is wrong on both counts.

MATERIALITY, measured on the policy-consistent arm (split-only MSH, the six failures + HEXAWARE cash-delisting + RAJESHEXPO kept, renames/swaps/demergers dropped per the shipped DROP policy), last-traded marks:
(a) MOVES. Deep-minus-shallow premium on median annualised excess — the metric RESULTS.md explicitly retreated to after retracting its first deep-bucket claim — goes from +3.9pp / +2.6pp / +4.5pp (hold / 24m / 36m) to -1.7pp / +0.4pp / -1.0pp. Hold-to-recovery DEEP falls +10.6%/yr -> +5.2%/yr while shallow is +6.9%/yr: deep is no longer better, it is worse. The "decisive table" arithmetic mean excess for DEEP collapses +41.4% -> +0.2%, all-entry -10.3% -> -19.3%, DEEP p10 net -14.5% -> -92.7%, DEEP recovery 76% -> 65%. Holds with IBREALEST added. Even the most generous restore (all 27, DROP policy ignored) only shrinks the premium to +1.5pp. The document's surviving position — "deep entries are modestly better" and "thinnest exactly where the edge is" — does not survive.
(b) CANNOT MOVE. report.py:88 builds pxc from S (charting) only; the portfolio sim never reads the bhavcopy panel. 20-slot hold-to-recovery is identical at 9.16% CAGR vs NIFTYBEES 10.27% in all five arms. Adding losers can only widen it. Note the same bias inflates the +12.04pp 10-slot/36-month number, which the sim fills deepest-first — DHFL at -92.9% off and HDIL at -73.6% off would have been top-ranked fills — so "a time stop makes it work" is also overstated, but that is not one of the three conclusions.
(c) STRENGTHENED, not moved.

Two fair caveats. The claimed counterfactual is asymmetric (detector kept on charting, dropped on bhavcopy) and the detector does have a real job there — bhavcopy never adjusts demergers — but none of the six names has a demerger or an in-hold split, so they are robust to that choice. And the auditor's quoted "+16.7% -> +15.8%" matches no figure I can produce (I get DEEP mean excess +0.2% policy / -2.1% six-only); their "<1pp" total-loss sensitivity is roughly right on the arithmetic metric but WRONG on the annualised one, because final2.py annx returns None when net <= -1, so total-loss marks silently drop those episodes and DEEP median annualised excess springs back to +10.6%. The last-traded mark is the arm to quote, which is what they did.

finding.title: The 54-episode deep bucket is a detector artefact — the honest count is 113–119, and the detector removes deep episodes at a higher rate than shallow
finding.claim: Conclusion (c) rests on "54 favourable episodes in 15.7 years (~3.4/year)". Under a CA-only arm (the study's own flags intersected with splits_calendar RAW/AMBIG ex-dates, plus the ITC demerger — identical truncation mechanics, false positives removed) the deep bucket is 107 charting episodes, 113 corrected, 119 with the restored failures: 7.6/year, not 3.4. The removal is selective: the detector drops 59 of 107 deep episodes (55%) but 141 of 346 shallow (41%), because a stock that is ≥35% off its 2-year high almost always got there via at least one ≥8% down day. Among passing signals the depth reading is also wrong — on the 6,838 slots where a false-positive flag lowered the high, measured "% off the high" is pulled UP by a median 18.9pp (p90 48.3pp) — but the damage is overwhelmingly deletion, not mis-measurement: only 2 passing signals change bucket.
finding.direction: Against conclusion (c)'s thinness argument. The sample-size objection to the deep bucket is substantially manufactured by the CA code.
finding.magnitude: Deep episode count 54 → 113 (corrected) / 119 (with restored failures), a 2.1–2.2× undercount. Deep removal rate 55% vs 41% shallow.
finding.where: study.py:102-143 candidates(); final.py:80-98 BUCK; RESULTS.md "Thin sample, and thinnest exactly where the edge is: ... only 54 in the deep bucket"

verdict.reasoning:
The factual core of the claim is real and I reproduced every number independently (scratchpad/ca_audit/refute.py, refute.log), but it moves none of (a), (b), (c).

REAL. study.py:83-99 is not a corporate-action correction, it is an idiosyncratic-crash filter: any single-day close-to-close drop <= -8% on a day NIFTY was not itself down >=4%, with no 50% bounce in 5 bars. That fires 2,722 times across 319 symbols. Intersected with splits_calendar RAW/AMBIG ex-dates plus the ITC demerger, only 63 flags across 53 symbols survive as genuine CAs. Because truncation moves w0 to the last flag and MIN_BARS=400 then rejects the slot out of a ~496-bar window, truncate behaves as exclude: 11,511 of 23,132 universe slots carry a flag, 10,183 are killed by MIN_BARS, and only 7 of the 253 base episodes actually trade on a truncated window. Deletion is selective exactly as claimed: deep 107 -> 48 (55% removed), shallow 346 -> 205 (41%). Deep goes 3.06/yr (base) to 6.82/yr (CA-only) to 7.39/yr (off). So "only 54 in the deep bucket (~3.4/year)" in RESULTS.md is a base-arm artefact quoted as if detector-independent.

RESTORATION IS LEGITIMATE, with a caveat. Of the 64 deep episodes CA-only restores, 51 (80%) actually regained the frozen 2-year high, so those highs were reachable and the flag was not a permanent level shift. 92% of the 158 governing flags sit in the -8%..-20% earnings-crash band; only 4% are worse than -30%. But CA-only is cleaner, not clean: splits_calendar carries no demergers, so a handful of restored entries are genuine level shifts (VEDL 2026-04-30 -64.9% Vedanta demerger, TATACHEM 2020-03-04 -56.5% Tata Consumer demerger, JISLJALEQS 2010-10-29 -79.6%). Honest deep count is ~100-113, not 113 exactly.

(a) NOT MOVED. On median annualised excess, the metric RESULTS.md itself adopted after retracting the mean-excess split, deep is +12.6%/yr base vs +12.4%/yr CA-only (unchanged), shallow +6.4% -> +8.6%, so the deep-shallow gap NARROWS from 6.2pp to 3.8pp. The top three episodes still account for 107% of the deep bucket's total arithmetic excess (HINDPETRO, CESC) at n=107 just as at n=48, so tripling the sample does not cure the tail dominance that already forced the retraction.

(b) NOT MOVED. The auditor only re-ran the bucket table; I ran the portfolio, which is the decisive aggregation. On the charting panel alone CA-only 20 slots does cross the index (10.83% vs 10.27%), but that crossing is an artefact of inconsistent survivorship treatment: the same CA filter was also deleting the delisted leg, and the CA-only arm leaves 50 survivorship episodes out of the book versus base's 13. Folding both legs into one book under matched detector philosophy (charting SH_CA + bhavcopy splits-only; union_pf.py), 20 slots is 7.95% base and 9.27% CA-only against NIFTYBEES 10.27% - still trails, and the headline number barely moves (9.16 -> 9.27). Forced delisting exits under CA-only: EDUCOMP -100, HDIL -100, OPTOCIRCUI -100, DHFL -100, ARSSINFRA -100, ABAN -93, RELINFRA -45. The 10-slot union book does improve (10.44% -> 15.20%, +4.93pp), and I am naming it rather than burying it, but (b) is explicitly about the diversified 20-slot case; 10 slots rests on 24 closed trades with 68% of terminal equity unrealised in GTL -85%, UCOBANK -78%, IDEA -72%, RPOWER -62% - the same "concentrate on the deepest" effect RESULTS.md already declined to count as independent.

(c) NOT MOVED. The thinness bullet is one of eight "Other known limits" and the headline three lines do not rest on it. Everything load-bearing holds or worsens under the cleaner detector: 20 slots still trails (-1.00pp); MDD still no better than the index (-35.17% vs -36.34%); concentration sensitivity gets worse (10-vs-20-slot spread 2.5pp -> 5.9pp); the "a time stop is what makes it work" headline collapses (10-slot/36m: 22.31% CAGR / MDD -27.66% / Calmar 0.81 -> 16.45% / -54.47% / 0.30); 60% of terminal equity is still unrealised; 2008 is still untestable; tail dominance survives. Clustering also partly survives: 23 of the 59 added deep episodes land in 2011 (+10) and 2020 (+13), independent entry years go 12 -> 15, though distinct deep symbols genuinely double, 36 -> 77.

PUSHBACK ON "MANUFACTURED". RESULTS.md already discloses that the detector flags "2,722 days across 319 symbols... too many for genuine corporate actions - it is catching earnings crashes" and already publishes the off arm at 459 episodes in the sensitivity table. The defect is narrower than claimed: the thinness bullet quotes the base-arm count alone without the detector-dependent range, and the sentence "Corporate-action handling does not drive the result" is false for the 10-slot/36-month headline - but it drives it toward MORE caution, which is why (c) survives.

FIX (documentation, not a re-run): reword the thinness bullet to "54 (base detector) to ~110 (CA-only) deep episodes over 15.7 years, detector-dependent", and qualify "CA handling does not drive the result" to note it does drive the 10-slot time-stop Calmar (0.81 -> 0.30) and MDD (-27.7% -> -54.5%).

finding.title: Conclusion (a)'s bucket split does not survive the CA correction: deep mean excess +41.4% → ~+14-17%, and the shallow band's "−23.5% destroys value" is −10.5%
finding.claim: Testing the specific claim (a): removing the detector's false positives moves the deep bucket from +41.4% to +25.4% mean excess and the shallow band from −23.5% to −10.5%; adding the 6 deleted survivorship failures takes the deep bucket to +13.8% (CA-only) or +16.7% (base arm). On median annualised excess — the one aggregation robust to both tails — the ordering actually INVERTS in the base arm once the deleted failures are restored: deep +4.5%/yr vs shallow +6.3%/yr. In the CA-only arm the gap is +10.5%/yr deep vs +8.3%/yr shallow, i.e. ~2pp/yr, not a categorical difference. A separate lens has already retracted (a) on tail-concentration grounds; this lens reaches the same verdict through a different mechanism and adds what tail-trimming cannot see — that the shallow band's apparent value destruction and the deep bucket's apparent strength are two faces of the same selection filter. (Tail dependence is confirmed under both CA arms: the top-3 deep episodes are 107% of total deep excess in each, and dropping them gives −5.1% base / −2.8% CA-only.)
finding.direction: Against the rule's reported edge concentration. Both halves of the quoted split are inflated by the CA code, in opposite directions.
finding.magnitude: Deep mean excess +41.4% → +13.8%/+16.7% (a 25–28pp overstatement). Shallow −23.5% → −10.5% (13pp overstatement of the damage). Deep median annualised excess +10.6%/yr → +4.5%/yr in the base arm with the deleted failures restored.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as stated, though the underlying mechanism is partly real.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Every number the auditor quotes is arithmetically correct. I rebuilt the hold-until-recovery bucket table from arm_episodes.json + kept_verified.json + surv_deleted_clean.json and got exact matches: shipped deep mean excess +41.4% / shallow -23.5%; CA-only +25.4% / -10.5%; base+6 deep +16.7%; CA-only+6 deep +13.8%; median annualised excess base+6 deep +4.5% vs shallow +6.3%, CA-only+6 +10.5% vs +8.3%. The CA mechanism is also real: study.py:114-120 truncates the 2y window at the last detected level shift and MIN_BARS=400 then rejects the slot, so on a ~500-bar window 'truncate' behaves close to 'exclude' (253 vs 233 vs 459 episodes across arms). And 6 genuine failures (EDUCOMP, ARSSINFRA, HDIL x2, OPTOCIRCUI, DHFL) were removed from the survivorship leg before the classifier saw them - a legitimate, previously-undisclosed omission worth a line in RESULTS.md's survivorship section.

WHY THE CLAIM STILL FAILS.

(1) The inversion is manufactured by a one-sided restoration. surv_deleted_clean.json holds 27 episodes the CA-correct arm produces, 16 of them deep. The auditor restored exactly the 6 deep catastrophes (median ann excess -53.7%/yr) and left out 10 deep episodes from the same file (median ann excess +28.7%/yr: EQUITAS, HEXAWARE x2, IBREALEST x2, RAJESHEXPO, MINDTREE, NIITTECH, INFRATEL, IBULHSGFIN) plus 11 shallow (+11.6%/yr). Shallow therefore received zero additions - the comparison denominator was never touched. Restoring all 27 (assumption-free bound, no classification needed) un-inverts the base arm: deep +8.9%/yr vs shallow +6.3%/yr, +2.6pp. The gap's sign flips across subsets of one file: -1.7 / +2.6 / -0.9pp.

(2) The gap is not estimable at this n in either direction. Bootstrap (20k resamples) 95% CI of the deep-minus-shallow median gap, base arm + the 6: [-8.8, +19.3]pp, P(deep>shallow)=41%. As-shipped: +4.3pp, CI [-5.1, +23.3]pp, P=69%. Deep-bucket ann-excess IQR is [-7.5, +40.2] (~48pp) on n=60. A 1.7pp median gap is ~1/28th of the bucket's own spread. 'The ordering actually INVERTS' is not a measurable fact; it is a coin flip.

(3) The inversion exists only in a mixed configuration - uncorrected charting leg bolted to a CA-corrected survivorship leg. The auditor's own preferred CA-only arm preserves the ordering under every restoration variant: +2.8 (shipped), +2.2 (+6), +2.5 (all 27), +2.6 (merge2-rule subset) pp.

(4) I also applied merge2's own DROP rule (rename/share-swap/demerger dropped) consistently, keeping the 6 plus HEXAWARE x3 and RAJESHEXPO: base arm deep +5.2 vs shallow +6.1, still marginally inverted at -0.9pp. I state this rather than bury it, but it does not rescue the claim - the sign is unstable across subsets, every CI spans zero by 15-28pp, and my classification of those 8 dropped symbols is from memory, so it is corroboration only. The all-27 bound is the load-bearing test and it un-inverts.

(5) On the metrics RESULTS.md:269 actually directs readers to use - deep median arithmetic excess and beat rate - nothing inverts at all: +26.3%/69% as shipped, +19.0%/62% with the 6, +23.0%/64% with all 27, against shallow's +10.6%/62% in every variant.

ALREADY DISCLOSED. The target text 'the rule's edge lives entirely in the deep bucket' appears in RESULTS.md only inside its own retraction. Line 110: 'Both numbers are artifacts and that conclusion does not stand.' Lines 132-133: 'deep entries are modestly better, not categorically different, and the shallow band is not value-destroying.' Lines 166-168 disown the mean-excess column under the survivorship table. Line 274 discloses the detector 'is catching earnings crashes' and that sensitivity arms (exclude 233 / off 459, line 196) do not drive the result. The claim's CA-only finding (+10.5 vs +8.3) is the document's own conclusion with a smaller gap. The auditor concedes the retraction.

NET: real mechanism, correct arithmetic, unsupported inference. The component carrying the 'material' severity - that both halves of the split are inflated and the ordering inverts - is refuted.

finding.title: Conclusion (b) is wrong in both directions: the −1.10pp shortfall is a detector artefact, and the 36-month-stop rescue the write-up now leads with collapses
finding.claim: The 20-slot hold-to-recovery figure (9.16% CAGR vs NIFTYBEES 10.27%, −1.10pp) is the capital-weighted number the updated RESULTS.md says is "the one to trust". Under the CA-only arm it is 10.83% vs 10.27% = +0.56pp — the sign flips. 10 slots goes 11.48% (+1.21pp) → 14.79% (+4.52pp). Read this as an upper bound, not a rehabilitation: portfolio() runs on the charting panel only, so no portfolio arm holds a survivorship name, and the deepest-first fill would have bought DHFL and HDIL. The more damaging half is the other direction: the 36-month-stop rescue (10 slots, 22.31% CAGR, MDD −27.66%, Calmar 0.81) becomes 16.45% CAGR, MDD −54.47%, Calmar 0.30 once the detector stops excluding crash-prone names, and 20 slots goes 14.64%/−35.09%/0.42 → 14.00%/−46.06%/0.30. The clean book ends holding GTL −85%, YESBANK −89%, IDEA −79%, RPOWER −74%, UCOBANK −78%. Episode-level drawdown stats are, by contrast, essentially unaffected (median MAE −22.5% → −22.9%, "fell a further ≥40%" 28% → 27%), so the risk understatement is a portfolio-level effect only.
finding.direction: Two-sided. The headline shortfall is too harsh (artefact); the time-stop fix is far too flattering — its drawdown is understated by ~27pp and its Calmar by 2.7×.
finding.magnitude: 20-slot edge −1.10pp → +0.56pp (1.7pp CAGR). 36m-stop 10-slot: CAGR −5.9pp, MDD 27pp worse (−27.66% → −54.47%), Calmar 0.81 → 0.30.

verdict.reasoning:
DEFECT IS REAL — I could not refute any part of it, and every number reproduces to the decimal in my own re-run (scratchpad/ref1/v1.py–v5.py, v1.log–v3.log, VERDICT.json).

MECHANISM CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY. I re-coded the flag classification rather than reusing the auditor's: of study.py's 2,722 SHIFTS flags, 2,623 (96.4%) match no fmp.splits_calendar ex-date within ±5 days and no dividend ≥4% of price; only 55 RAW + 7 AMBIG splits and 29 big dividends are explained. 561 flags land on days NIFTYBEES itself fell 2–4%, i.e. inside the IDX_OK=−4% gate. The flags on the five names at issue are textbook credit/earnings crashes with ZERO split matches across all 92 of their flags: YESBANK −29% on 2018-09-21 (RBI cut Rana Kapoor's term) and −29% on 2019-04-30, GTL −62% on 2011-06-20, RPOWER −35% on 2019-02-04, UCOBANK/IDEA similar. And "truncate" is "exclude": candidates() sets w0=max(w0, sh.max()) then skips on MIN_BARS=400, so of 11,511 flagged slot-evaluations (out of 23,132), 9,961 (86.5%) are DELETED and only 1,328 actually truncate. Signals 1,146 → 2,416 (CA-only) / 2,478 (ca_mode='off'); episodes 253 → 453 / 459.

IT DOESN'T DEPEND ON THE AUDITOR'S CUSTOM ARM. The study's own shipped ca_mode='off' brackets it: 20-slot hold 11.52% (+1.25pp), 10-slot 36m-stop 13.42% / MDD −53.90% / Calmar 0.25. So RESULTS.md's sensitivity-section line "Corporate-action handling does not drive the result" is true at episode level and FALSE at portfolio level — the level the same document calls "the one to trust." That is the defect in one sentence.

(b) DOES NOT MOVE — the sign flip is itself an artefact and I measured it away. portfolio() runs on the charting panel, which is missing 112 universe symbols, so the deepest-first fill can never buy the names the crash detector deleted from the survivorship leg. I merged them in at bhavcopy prices (epochs normalised by −66,600 s; 4,211/4,215 land exactly on the charting/index grid) with split-only shift sets. CA-only 20-slot hold goes 10.83% (+0.56pp) → 10.18% (−0.09pp) with the 5 deleted failures, −0.09pp with the study's own 6 added too, −0.75pp with no bhav truncation, −0.24pp with all 112 symbols; a sibling session's independent implementation (j3.log, not mine) got −0.99pp. Every treatment is negative, i.e. back where the shipped −1.10pp was. v5.py isolates it: the move is driven entirely by ARSSINFRA (−92%, insolvency) and HDIL (−97%, NCLT, equity extinguished); OPTOCIRCUI's split-during-hold has zero effect on the 20-slot result, so the bound isn't an unadjusted-price artefact. The claim pre-conceded this ("an upper bound, not a rehabilitation") — I confirmed the bound. Separately, +0.56pp with 53% of final equity unrealised in GTL −87%, YESBANK −89%, IDEA −79%, RPOWER −74%, UCOBANK −78% is not a beat under any reading.

The 10-slot counterargument also fails. CA-only 10-slot hold stays +4.52pp and barely moves with survivorship (+4.25 to +4.52) — but it rests on 19 closed trades in 15.7 years with 46% of final equity unrealised in GTL −85% / UCOBANK −78% / IDEA −72% / RPOWER −62%, the exact basis on which RESULTS.md already dismissed the 5-slot 18.33% as "not a result"; and it is unstable to the bhav shift treatment (+4.52 → +1.73 when one more name gets bought). RESULTS.md stated (b) for the diversified 20-slot book, with the shipped 10-slot already at +1.21pp.

(a) DOES NOT MOVE. Median annualised excess, deep ≤−35% vs shallow: 12.6 vs 6.4 %/yr (shipped), 12.4 vs 8.6 (CA-only), 10.9 vs 9.0 (off). Deep stays modestly better in every arm and the gap narrows under the clean arms — the same direction RESULTS.md already retracted toward ("modestly better, not categorically different"). No reversal.

(c) IS REINFORCED, NOT MOVED. The version RESULTS.md says works degrades monotonically as the data gets cleaner. 10-slot 36m-stop Calmar: 0.81 → 0.30 (CA-only) → 0.27 (+5 failures) → 0.24 (+ study's 6) → 0.19 (all 112), with MDD −27.66% → −54.47% → −64.51%. 20-slot vs index: +4.37pp → +3.73 → +2.89 → +0.99 → −1.00pp, i.e. the "rescue" ends up BELOW the index with full survivorship. Timing: peak 2019-04-15 → trough 2020-03-23 (NBFC/credit crisis into COVID), and 2019 standalone is −19% for the clean 10-slot book in a year the index rose — so it isn't a single COVID artefact.

DIRECTION: the claim calls itself two-sided; in effect it is one-sided. The "headline shortfall too harsh" half dies under survivorship; only the "time-stop far too flattering" half survives, and it is worse than claimed.

MATERIALITY, by the task's own rule: real but moves none of (a)/(b)/(c), so not material to the conclusion — it strengthens the "don't" answer. It is still worth a correction to RESULTS.md on three lines: (1) point 2's "22.31% / −27.66% / Calmar 0.81 / +12.04pp" rescue is not robust (0.30 clean, 0.19 survivorship-corrected); (2) point 3's "Drawdown never improves on the index (−27.7% to −38.0%)" — clean arms are −46% to −64%; (3) the sensitivity-section claim that CA handling doesn't drive the result, which is false at portfolio level.

finding.title: The sensitivity arm offered as proof that CA handling is immaterial never tests the claim it is cited for
finding.claim: RESULTS.md asserts "Corporate-action handling does not drive the result" and "Sensitivity arms show it does not drive the result", citing exclude/off at 233/459 episodes with median excess +15.4%/+19.0%. That row reports MEDIAN excess for ALL entries. The headline conclusion is a MEAN-excess split BY off-high bucket, and that split was never computed under any CA arm other than `truncate` — final.py imports `C` from variants.py, which is hard-wired to `ca_mode='truncate'`. When you do compute it: all-entry mean excess −10.3% → −1.8%, shallow −23.5% → −10.5%, deep count 54 → 113. The median-excess row is genuinely stable (+14.0% → +19.0%) precisely because medians are insensitive to the composition change the arms create, so it cannot detect the thing it is quoted as ruling out. The paired `exclude` arm adds nothing independent either (finding #2).
finding.direction: FAVOURS the rule — a robustness check that cannot fail is reported as a robustness check that passed.
finding.magnitude: The untested quantity moves by 8.5pp (all-entry mean excess), 13pp (shallow), 16pp (deep) and 2.1× (deep n) across the arms the sensitivity row claims to cover.
finding.where: variants.py:9-11 (BASE hard-wires ca_mode='truncate'); final.py:7 `from variants import walk2, BASE, C`; main.py:43-44 arm() reports medians only; RESULTS.md Sensitivity table and its closing line
finding.empirical: Ran the full final.py bucket table under truncate / exclude / off / CA-only. The median-excess column moves +14.0 → +15.4 → +19.0 → +17.1 while mean excess moves −2.0 → +2.1 → +4.7 → +3.1 and deep n moves 48 → 46 → 116 → 107. scratchpad/ca_audit/run.py section 6.

verdict.which_conclusion: (b) FLIPS SIGN under both doc-named arms — 20-slot hold-to-recovery is -1.10pp vs NIFTYBEES only under `truncate`; it is +2.95pp under `exclude` and +1.25pp under `off`. (a) strong form ("edge is only in deep <=-35%") is not robust — the deep-vs-shallow ordering on median annualised excess inverts under `exclude` (+5.0 vs +8.2) — but the weak form the doc actually retains ("modestly better, not categorically different") is unmoved. (c) SURVIVES and is reinforced: under `off` the bolded 10-slot/36m-stop fix collapses from 22.31%/MDD -27.66%/Calmar 0.81 to 13.42%/MDD -53.90%/Calmar 0.25.
verdict.reasoning:
STRUCTURAL CLAIM: confirmed by reading the code. `variants.py:9-10` hard-wires `ca_mode='truncate'` in BASE and binds `C=candidates(**BASE)` at import (line 11); `final.py:7` does `from variants import walk2, BASE, C`, so the entire bucket x exit-rule grid — the table RESULTS.md calls "the decisive table" — only ever ran under truncate. `main.py`'s `arm()` (lines 25-37) emits medNet/medExcess/medMAE/medDays and nothing else: no mean, no bucket split, no portfolio. So the CA rows at main.py:43-44, and the RESULTS.md sensitivity row they feed (exclude/off, 233/459 episodes, med excess +15.4%/+19.0%), are median-excess-for-all-entries only. The two sentences they are quoted to support — "Corporate-action handling does not drive the result" and "Sensitivity arms show it does not drive the result" — are not supported by that row.

MEASURED (ref2.py; my harness reproduces the shipped truncate row exactly — 266/212/54 episodes, mean excess -10.3/-23.5/+41.4, median annualised 7.4/6.7/10.6 — so the other arms are trustworthy). Survivorship-corrected, hold-to-recovery, truncate -> exclude -> off:
  median excess (all):  +12.2 -> +15.1 -> +17.8   (the row the doc quotes: stable, 5.6pp span)
  MEAN excess (all):    -10.3 ->  -7.2 ->  -0.2   (10.1pp, sign flip)
  MEAN excess (shallow):-23.5 -> -19.0 -> -10.3
  episodes:              266  ->  246  ->  472
  DEEP n:                 54  ->   52  ->  122    (+126%)
The claim's mechanism is exactly right: the median is insensitive to the composition change the arms create, so it cannot detect the thing it is quoted as ruling out. Finding #2 is also confirmed — `exclude` adds almost nothing per-episode (deep n 54->52, signals 1146->1055, open book nearly identical per ref3.log).

THE SHARPEST PROOF OF MATERIALITY: `exclude` is statistically indistinguishable from `truncate` on every per-episode measure, yet 20-slot hold-to-recovery moves 4.06pp (9.16% -> 13.22%) and crosses the index. 91 differing monthly signals swing the number RESULTS.md calls "the one headline number that is capital-weighted ... so it is the one to trust." The doc's own "concentration-sensitive, high variance, not a robust edge" caveat applies to the one line that was supposed to be immune to it.

DIRECTION: the claim's "FAVOURS the rule" is wrong — it is MIXED. `truncate` is the HARSHEST arm on per-episode mean excess (-10.3 vs -0.2) and on headline #1 (the only arm where 20 slots trails the index), and the MOST FLATTERING arm only on the bolded 10-slot/36m line (+12.04pp vs +3.15pp under `off`, Calmar 0.81 vs 0.25). Also, the claim's quoted figures (-1.8 / -10.5 / deep 113) are from the prior auditor's invented CA-ONLY arm, not from the doc's `off` (-0.2 / -10.3 / deep 122) — same magnitudes, mislabelled arm.

CONCLUSION vs DECISION: (b) flips as a stated fact, but the bottom line does not. There is no arm where both halves of the doc's story hold: in `off`, where hold-to-recovery goes positive, the time-stop fix the doc proposes blows MDD out to -53.90%. The answer "does not clear the bar" stands; the specific sentences supporting it do not.
verdict.empirical_check: Ran .venv/bin/python on ca_audit/ref2.py and ref3.py (logs: ca_audit/ref2.log, ref3.log; data: ref2_out.json, ref2_verdict.json). ref2.py re-ran candidates() under ca_mode in {truncate, exclude, off}, fed each through walk2 + episodes + the survivorship fold-in held fixed (final.py's MC/mwalk2 verbatim), and reported mean AND median excess, bucket counts, median annualised excess, plus portfolio() hold-to-recovery and pf() 24m/36m time stops at 10 and 20 slots for every arm. Truncate row reproduces RESULTS.md exactly, validating the harness. Portfolio vs NIFTYBEES (pp): hold-to-recovery 20 slots -1.10 / +2.95 / +1.25; 10 slots +1.21 / +0.12 / +2.29; 36m-stop 10 slots +12.04 / +9.68 / +3.15 (MDD -27.66 / -25.83 / -53.90); 24m-stop 10 slots +10.10 / +12.73 / +0.91 (MDD -37.98 / -33.93 / -52.47). ref3.py confirmed the exclude-vs-truncate flip is not a value-trap-exclusion artefact: UCOBANK/UNIONBANK/PNB/IDBI/IDEA remain in the exclude book. Validity of using the `off` arm at all: prior refute.log section 2 shows 51 of 64 deep highs restored by dropping truncation were actually regained (80%), so those targets are reachable prices and not permanent corporate-action level shifts; section 8 shows only 12 of 459 `off` episodes have a raw/ambiguous split in window (median excess +19.0 -> +17.5 without them), so `off` is not materially split-contaminated.

audit.lens: BENCHMARK AND RETURN ACCOUNTING — symmetry of the stock leg vs NIFTYBEES, the cost model, the dividend leg, per-trade excess construction, and right-censoring.

findings.title: The dividend leg is inflated ~86x on a subset of rows; it single-handedly manufactures the deep-bucket edge

HINDPETRO 2021-07-08 is booked at Rs 1,314.93 against a Rs 189.23 share price (695% in one payment). The multiplier recovers exactly as 86.197 (ARVIND Rs 1.00 -> 86.197; DRREDDY Rs 11.25 -> 971.80), i.e. an INR-value-treated-as-USD conversion; that mechanism is a hypothesis, but the SCALE DEFECT itself is verified independently against the market: on the flagged ex-dates the observed one-day price fall matches value/86.197 in 98 of 124 rows (HINDPETRO 2021-07-08 actually fell Rs 15.00; repaired value Rs 15.25). This is a warehouse-wide fmp.dividend_calendar defect, not a study bug — it hits any NSE backtest using adjDividend.

findings.title: Idle cash earns 0% in the portfolio sim while the benchmark is 100% invested — 33-40% of the book
findings.claim: report.py portfolio() keeps unspent capital in a `cash` variable that accrues nothing ('cash earns nothing' is stated, not justified), then compares the blended result to a fully-invested NIFTYBEES. The rule structurally cannot fill its slots: time-weighted mean cash is 33.2% at 10 slots and 35.6% at 20 slots (median ~40%), and only 5-8 entries were ever blocked by the `cash < alloc*0.999` break — so this is genuine candidate scarcity, not an implementation artefact. Conclusion (b)'s headline 9.16% vs 10.27% is therefore a part-cash portfolio measured against an all-equity index, and the -1.10pp margin is smaller than the accounting error.
findings.where: report.py:78,89,101,106,114-119 portfolio(); variants.py:49,65,77-78 pf()
findings.direction: Against the rule. It makes the published numbers too harsh and challenges (b) as stated — though it is more than offset by the dividend defect.
findings.magnitude: With published dividends: 20 slots 9.16% -> 10.83% at 5%/yr cash (sign of the index gap FLIPS to +0.56pp), 11.43% at 6.5%, 12.68% with cash parked in NIFTYBEES (+2.41pp). With dividends repaired: 20 slots 6.78% -> 8.19% / 8.65% / 10.01%. The honest head-to-head — repaired dividends and cash parked in NIFTYBEES, which is the stated alternative — is 10.01% vs NIFTYBEES 10.27% at 20 slots and 11.29% vs 10.27% at 10 slots. So the true margin is +-1pp, i.e. at par, and the published -1.10pp is a coincidence of two offsetting errors each 2-4x its size.
findings.empirical: pf_audit.py and verify.py: re-implemented portfolio() faithfully (base case reproduces 11.48%/9.16%, MDD -31.30%/-29.75%, closed 21/46 exactly), then added instrumentation for time-weighted cash share, blocked-entry count and slot-full count, and three alternative cash treatments: daily accrual at 5.0%/yr, at 6.5%/yr, and cash held as NIFTYBEES units sold at that day's close (0.15% cost applied to the ETF trades, which is conservative since the benchmark pays none). Ran the full grid x {10,20} slots x {hold-to-recovery, 24m, 36m} x {published, repaired} dividends.

findings.title: The published max drawdown is cash-damped, so conclusion (c)'s risk numbers are not comparable to the index's
findings.claim: The -29.75% MDD for the 20-slot book is measured on a portfolio that is ~36% cash, against a 100%-invested index at -36.34%. The quoted range '-27.7% to -38.0% vs -36.34%' actually contains rows that BEAT the index, which contradicts the sentence 'Drawdown never improves on the index' it is cited to support. Once the accounting is symmetric the answer is cash-treatment dependent, and no single number should be quoted as 'the' drawdown.
findings.where: report.py:124-128 (mdd vs b_mdd computed on curves with different invested fractions); RESULTS.md 'Drawdown is no better than the index' and headline #3
findings.direction: The published number flatters the rule's risk. The conclusion (c) is right in spirit but for the wrong reason, and the honest equity-sleeve figure is much worse than stated.
findings.magnitude: Repaired dividends + cash at 5-6.5%/yr: MDD -30.5% to -33.2%, i.e. BETTER than the index (Calmar 0.44-0.47 vs the index's 0.28). Repaired + cash parked in NIFTYBEES (all-equity, apples-to-apples): -40.65% at 20 slots, -43.46% at 10, and -45.69% / -48.42% with a 36-month stop — materially WORSE than -36.34%. Defensible statement: the equity sleeve drew down worse than the index; the blended book's MDD is set by 35-40% scarcity cash and is not a comparable risk measure.
findings.empirical: Same grid as the finding above (pf_audit.py, verify.py). MDD recomputed on each equity curve as (eq/cummax(eq)-1).min(), with the index MDD recomputed on nb_c over the identical date range, for every combination of dividend treatment x cash treatment x slots x exit rule.

findings.title: The survivorship leg is credited zero dividends while the charting leg is credited dividends — the 266-row mean mixes two return definitions
findings.claim: surv.py:93 and final.py:27 compute net=(x_px*(1-COST))/(e_px*(1+COST))-1 with divd hard-coded to 0.0, and the folded episodes are held 0.8-14.3 years. findings.title: Terminal names stop accruing index opportunity cost at their last print, truncating the excess comparison
findings.claim: For an open trade walk() sets x_d to the stock's last bar and measures the benchmark over e_d..x_d. For 9 of the 53 open episodes the stock's series ends 0.6-4.5 years before the data edge (RELINFRA x2 2025-06, BGRENERGY 2026-02, RCOM 2022-05, SINTEX x5 2022-03), so the index leg is frozen at the delisting date rather than running to today. Note the 'right' convention is genuinely ambiguous without a redeployment rule, so this is a disclosure issue rather than a clear error.
findings.where: study.py:155-173 walk() (x_d = last forward bar); surv.py:90-96; merge2.py table() pools both into one mean
findings.direction: Favours the rule on the terminal names (RCOM, SINTEX) and against it on the two 2025/2026 stubs, because the index itself fell 12.9% in 2026. Net: favours the rule.

Re-run with the real open flag gives 9 rows and -1.58pp.

findings.title: Cost model, dividend near-duplicates, bar alignment and the NIFTYBEES total-return assumption are all verified immaterial
findings.claim: The four items the brief asked me to confirm all check out. (1) Cost model: 0.15%/side is adequate — the statutory Indian delivery round trip is ~0.22% today (STT 0.10% each side, stamp duty 0.015% on buy, exchange ~0.003%, SEBI + GST on the small components) and ~0.27% before the June-2013 STT cut, both inside the 0.30% round trip assumed, and the rule's turnover is far too low for it to matter. The benchmark pays no cost at all, worth ~0.3pp per trade in the rule's favour to concede. (2) The known dividend near-duplicate defect is real and immaterial: 34 rows <=1 day apart = 0.53% of rows and 0.44% of rupee value — confirmed, and utterly dwarfed by the 86x scale defect in the same field. (3) Benchmark bar alignment is clean: zero real mismatches. The 13 apparent ones are floor-division artefacts of the bhavcopy 03:30 epoch offset; the worst genuine gap is 2 days (a SINTEX exit dated on a Sunday). (4) NIFTYBEES IS a fair accumulating total-return benchmark, so the write-up's assumption holds.
findings.where: study.py:146 COST, study.py:167-168 bi/bj construction, pull.py step 6 (duplicates), pull.py step 4 (benchmark)
findings.direction: All four either favour nothing or are mildly conservative (against the rule). None challenges any conclusion.
findings.magnitude: Costs: raising COST from 0.15% to 0.50% per side moves the 20-slot CAGR from 9.16% to 9.00% (-0.16pp) and the 10-slot from 11.48% to 11.33%. Duplicates: 0.44% of dividend value. Alignment: <=0.2% of index return on 13 of 266 rows. Benchmark: no detectable dividend leakage, so no correction.

(2) div_audit.py grouped divs.json by symbol and counted rows <=1 day apart, valuing the overlap at the smaller of the pair. (3) bench_audit.py asserted nb_d[searchsorted(nb_d,e_d,'left')] == e_d and nb_d[searchsorted(nb_d,x_d,'right')-1] == x_d for all 266 rows and printed every gap. (4) Pulled daily closes for 12 Nifty-50 ETFs from nse.nse_charting_day and compared NIFTYBEES year by year to the median peer 2012-2026: diffs -1.64pp to +1.33pp, median ~0.0pp, with no single year showing a ~-1.3% dividend-leak shortfall; NIFTYBEES also beats the KNOWN-distributing SETFNIF50 by +0.62%/yr over 11.2 years, about equal to SETFNIF50's five declared distributions. Separately, fmp.dividend_calendar carries zero NIFTYBEES rows (correctly) while carrying SETFNIF50's five. The large negative CAGRs for BSLNIFTY/IVZINNIFTY/NIFTY1 are unadjusted-split artefacts in those peer series, not evidence.

findings.title: OUT OF LENS but found: EPS and the adjusted price are on inconsistent bases, so the multiple gates are contaminated
findings.claim: The same class of defect as finding 1 sits in the selection leg. nse_charting_day divides historical prices by the cumulative factor of splits that occur AFTER the date, while fmp.income_statement eps is the as-filed per-share figure and is not restated. pe_now = adjusted_price / unrestated_eps is therefore too LOW for any name with large post-date splits, and the pe_now <= 60x / pe_need <= 35x gates admit names they should reject. FEDERALBNK appears with pe_now = 1.03 (adjusted price Rs 5.12 against eps Rs 4.98); HINDPETRO — the name that drives the deep bucket — appears at pe_now 3.08-3.91 against split factors of 3:1 (2016) x 3:2 (2017) x 3:2 (2024) = 6.75x.
findings.where: study.py:129-130 pe_now = px_t/eps_now and pe_need = hi/eps_now, with px_t/hi from adjusted charting and eps_now from pull.py step 5
findings.direction: Loosens the two multiple filters, i.e. admits candidates the stated rule excludes. Direction of effect on returns unmeasured; it means the tested rule is not the specified rule.
findings.magnitude: Not measured — outside my lens. Scope indicator: 4 of 1,146 signals have pe_now < 2 and the p1 is 2.49 against a median of 10.12, so the grossly impossible cases are few, but any name with a post-date split carries a proportional understatement and HINDPETRO (6.75x) is among them. The right fix is to restate eps by the same cumulative factor the price series uses, or to compute pe from unadjusted bhavcopy prices.
findings.empirical: Ran candidates() under the base config and printed the pe_now distribution over all 1,146 signals: min 1.03, p1 2.49, median 10.12, max 25.01; listed every signal with pe_now < 2 and every distinct HINDPETRO (pe_now, eps) pair. Cross-checked against fmp.splits_calendar for HINDPETRO (3:2 1999, 3:1 2016-09-14, 3:2 2017-07-11, 3:2 2024-06-21).

audit.verdict_on_conclusion:
This lens FALSIFIES (a) and leaves (b) and (c) standing but with both headline numbers wrong in ways that happen to offset.

(a) — FALSIFIED, and more damningly than the write-up's own in-flight retraction. RESULTS.md now says the +41.4% vs -23.5% split is a fat-tail artefact and replaces it with median annualised excess (DEEP +10.6%/yr vs shallow +6.7%/yr, "deep entries are modestly better"). verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The defect is real at source, real against the market, and it is the entire source of conclusion (a).

EXISTENCE — confirmed in the warehouse, not inferred. A live query of fmp.dividend_calendar returns ARVIND.NS 2012-09-13 with dividend = adjDividend = 86.197000 against a true FY12 DPS of Rs 1.00, and the series continues exactly: 142.22505/86.197 = 1.65000, then 2.35 / 2.40 / 2.40 / 2.40 / 2.00. The corruption also stops: 2025-26 rows are sane (ARVIND 3.75/4.50, HINDPETRO 10.5/5.0/19.25, DRREDDY 8.0), so this is a historical-backfill defect. Both `dividend` and `adjDividend` carry it, so the raw column is not a repair path. Warehouse-wide scope: 469 rows across 192 .NS symbols (of 26,752 / 2,059) carry the exact 86.197 signature, and that is a lower bound because it misses HINDPETRO's own worst row. Not a study bug.

SCALE — verified independently against price. HINDPETRO's adjusted charting close went 204.2333 -> 189.2333 on 2021-07-08, a fall of exactly Rs 15.00, against a booked dividend of Rs 1,314.93 and a repaired value of Rs 15.255. Across the 47 rows worth >50% of the share price, 46 of 47 one-day falls sit closer to value/86.197 than to the published value; across 124 rows >8%, 98 of 124. And adjDividend/86.197 (15.255) is the right basis, not dividend/86.197 (22.88) — FMP's bonus adjustment sits on the same footing as nse_charting_day. A cash dividend 7x the share price is impossible on its face; the price test only pins the repair.

MATERIALITY — this is where I expected the claim to fail, and it did not. I reproduced the published base exactly (meanExc hold: all -10.3% / shallow -23.5% / DEEP +41.4%, n = 266/212/54) and then re-walked the identical episode set under four repairs plus a no-dividends bound. Only 6 of 253 episodes have any changed dividend credit, but they carry 51.8% of all rupee dividend credited, and 3 of them are HINDPETRO in the DEEP bucket. HINDPETRO 2018-08-01 alone goes from +1956.3% net to +98.2% — 1,858pp of fabricated return in one episode out of 54. The DEEP bucket's sum of net returns falls from 7,102pp to 3,570pp.

On the headline metric the deep-vs-shallow separation is 100% artifact: the DEEP-minus-shallow meanExc gap goes from +64.9pp to +0.5pp (repair >50%), -0.9pp (>8%), -0.3pp (zero), -4.7pp (no divs). On the median annualised excess that final2.py switched to precisely because of outlier domination, the gap does not merely narrow, it inverts: DEEP +10.6% vs shallow +6.7% becomes DEEP +5.2% vs shallow +6.4%. Only the trimmed annualised mean keeps a deep tilt, halved (+9.6pp -> +5.0pp). The decision-relevant form of (a) — just trade the deep ones — flips sign in the portfolio: DEEP-only 20 slots goes 13.57% (+3.30pp over NIFTYBEES) to 7.41% (-2.86pp), and 10 slots +0.59pp to -4.42pp. Three of four metrics plus the portfolio kill (a). It does not survive.

(b) and (c) are not moved, because the defect only ever flattered the rule — but they are reinforced, and one number matters: the 5-slot portfolio's +8.06pp edge, the single strongest-looking piece of evidence against (b) in the published output, collapses to +0.34pp (and to -1.74pp with dividends off). At 10 and 20 slots the rule goes from +1.21pp / -1.10pp to -2.25pp / -3.37pp, with MDD worsening from -31.30% to -35.13%. The repair is threshold-insensitive — 50% / 20% / 8% / flagged-to-zero agree within 0.2pp in every cell — so nothing here depends on where the line is drawn.

The auditor's characterisation is accurate, including "the entire source of conclusion (a)". The one thing I would add: killing (a) removes the study's last positive finding, so the corrected reading is not "the edge is shallow too" but "there is no edge in either bucket held to recovery" — which makes (b) and (c) the only conclusions left standing.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. I could not refute any part of it — every number the claim asserts reproduced exactly.

CODE IS AS DESCRIBED. report.py:106 `cash=start`, :89 `cash += p['alloc']*(1+net)`, :119 `cash-=alloc`. There is no accrual term anywhere in portfolio(); the docstring's "cash earns nothing" is a bare assertion. The `edge` print (report.py:135-139) sets that part-cash curve against `nb_c` buy & hold, fully invested, same window. variants.py pf() (:49,65,77-78) carries the identical treatment.

MEASUREMENTS (base case reproduced to the cent first — 18.33/11.48/9.16% CAGR, MDD -37.13/-31.30/-29.75%, closed 15/21/46, final 14.05/5.51/3.96x at 5/10/20 slots; no variant was believed until that matched):
- Time-weighted cash share: 22.5% / 33.2% / 35.6% at 5/10/20 slots; medians 23.2% / 40.0% / 40.5%. The claim's "33.2% at 10, 35.6% at 20, median ~40%" is exact.
- Blocked by `cash < alloc*0.999`: 5 at 10 slots, 8 at 20 slots — exactly the claimed 5-8. (The claim omits 5 slots, where it is 26; irrelevant to (b).)

SO IT IS A REAL DEFECT, though not a bug: the behaviour is what the code says. What makes it a defect is the comparison — a one-third-cash portfolio scored against an all-equity index with neither side adjusted.

MECHANISM IS MORE PRECISE THAN THE CLAIM STATES. At 20 slots, slots were full on 128/186 decision dates, the candidate list exhausted on 41/186, and cash blocked only 8/186, with 19.0 of 20 slots held on average. So slots were the binding constraint on 69% of dates while 36% of capital sat idle. The cause is not plain candidate scarcity: it is the fixed-slot / never-rebalanced sizing plus median ~20-month holds. Exits return 1+net times a stale `alloc`, new entries take only eq/slots, and existing positions are never topped up, so cash accumulates that the rule structurally cannot deploy. Same conclusion (zero yield on it is an avoidable measurement choice), but the parent needs the right cause if they are deciding whether to redesign sizing.

MOVES (b). Published (b) rests on one number, the 20-slot -1.10pp; 5 and 10 slots were already +8.06pp and +1.21pp. That number flips sign under every cash treatment: +0.56pp at 5.0%/yr, +1.17pp at 6.5%/yr, +2.41pp parked in NIFTYBEES (moved +1.66 / +2.27 / +3.52pp). The claim's "margin smaller than the accounting error" is measured, not rhetorical.

But with magnitude honesty: +0.56pp at the conservative post-tax liquid-fund floor is indistinguishable from zero on 46 closed trades, one path, with 67% of terminal equity unrealised. And under ETF parking — the stated deployment — MDD goes -29.75% -> -38.36%, WORSE than the index's -36.34% (Calmar 0.33 vs index 0.28). So the published 20-slot drawdown advantage was itself a cash-cushion artefact, which cuts against the rule and the claim did not mention. Replacement (b): "hold-to-recovery ties to modestly beats NIFTYBEES at 20 slots, with no risk-adjusted advantage once idle cash is honestly deployed; at 5/10 slots it was already ahead."

ONE LEG OF (b) SURVIVES: the event-study mean excess for hold-to-recovery episodes is -2.0% (main.log) — per-trade, over each trade's own window, no cash in it. I knocked out the portfolio leg of (b), not the per-trade leg.

DOES NOT MOVE (a). (a) is an event-study conclusion with no cash in it. I measured the one place cash could interact — the portfolio-level all-vs-deep ordering — and it is unchanged in sign at every slot count under all three treatments: deep-minus-all = -3.42/-2.84/-1.19pp at 5 slots, -0.62/-1.53/-1.36pp at 10, +4.40/+4.10/+3.04pp at 20. The index is 100% invested at both points. Cause is structural, not incidental: report.py:89 cash earns 0, :110 breaks on `len(pos)>=slots` regardless of idle cash, :114 sets alloc=eq/slots at entry so shrunken losers are never topped up. The 100%-invested-equivalent sleeve (time-weighted, positions held across each day boundary) draws down **-49.31%** vs the index's -36.34% — 13pp WORSE where the published figure is 6.6pp BETTER, a 19.6pp swing. **Leg 3 — cash-treatment dependence: confirmed.** Same 20-slot hold book, MDD by convention alone: rf 6% -24.10% / idle 0% -29.75% (published) / cash in NIFTYBEES -38.29% / sleeve only -49.31%. A 25.2pp spread. "No single number should be quoted as 'the' drawdown" is correct.

**Materiality — it moves (b), in the direction the auditor did NOT claim.** RESULTS.md:13-17 calls 20-slot hold "9.16% CAGR against NIFTYBEES's 10.27%" (-1.10pp) "the one headline number... the one to trust." That shortfall is entirely the cash drag: the stock sleeve compounds at 14.12%/yr and 9.16% = 64.4% x 14.12% + 35.6% x 0% (the decomposition reconciles exactly - 0.644x14.12 + 0.356x10.27 = 12.75% matches the measured cash-in-index CAGR to 2dp). Under symmetric cash the -1.10pp becomes rf +1.01pp (tautology-proof: cash in a liquid fund, not in the benchmark) and index-cash +2.48pp. Against a total-return benchmark (+1.2-1.5%/yr) those become rf -0.30pp and index-cash +1.69/+1.49pp. Honest symmetric range: **-0.3pp to +2.5pp, centred ~+1pp**. So the correct statement is not "it beats the index" but "it is indistinguishable from the index and the sign depends on the convention" — which still moves (b), because the published form is a confident specific figure at the pessimistic extreme, labelled as the number to trust. Turning the stock-leg dividends off as well (both legs price-only) gives -1.40pp, so the sign is jointly cash- and dividend-dependent, exactly as claimed.

Secondary, feeding the same point: the benchmark is NIFTYBEES *close* with no dividends added (pull.py:81-84) while the stock leg does add them (study.py:163, report.py:92). pull.py asserts "NIFTYBEES reinvests," but NIFTYBEES/Nifty-50 was ~1/100 in Jan-2011 (55.468 vs ~5,505) and pull.py's own construction adds nothing, so nb_c looks price-like. I treat the 1.2-1.5% uplift as a sensitivity, not a measured correction (the 2026 end-ratio check is circular and I did not pin it down).

**(c) is not moved — strengthened, and the claim's "right in spirit, wrong reason" is correct.** Once symmetric, risk-adjusted return is a wash: 20-slot hold sleeve Calmar 0.29 vs index 0.28; index-cash blend 0.36 vs TRI-index 0.32. So "not a lower-risk alternative" holds, but for the opposite reason to the one given — the sleeve drawdown is -49%, not a flattering -30%. **(a) is untouched** and was already self-retracted in RESULTS.md:106-135.

Notably the fix does NOT collapse headline #2: the 10-slot/36-month row survives symmetric accounting largely intact (sleeve Calmar 0.82, sleeve MDD -31.07% vs published -27.66%). What collapses is the confident negative on the base case and the "no risk-reduction" phrasing.

Needs rewriting (I did not edit RESULTS.md; the parent aggregates): lines 13-17 (headline #1), 22 (headline #3), 272, and the MDD column of the portfolio table at 210-219 should carry the invested fraction or be stated per cash convention. Separately, and not mixing baselines: on the sibling session's corrected panel (scratchpad/bcbt/fixed_pf.log, delisted names buyable and marked to zero) 20-slot hold is already +1.36pp under idle cash — the two corrections compound in the same direction.

finding.title: OUT OF LENS but found: EPS and the adjusted price are on inconsistent bases, so the multiple gates are contaminated

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on premise, magnitude and both cited exhibits.

PREMISE FALSE. The claim rests on "fmp.income_statement eps is the as-filed per-share figure and is not restated". It is retro-restated. FV-free test (does N_eps = ni/eps jump by the split factor at the first fiscal year on/after each ex-date, over 482 universe split events): 370 RESTATED (76.8%), 42 as-filed (8.7%, nearly all factors 1.01-1.12 = ordinary issuance, not splits), 70 ambiguous (14.5%).

EXHIBIT 1 (HINDPETRO) WRONG BY 4.5x. As-filed FY2010 count = commonStock 3.390bn / FV 10 = 339M; the eps field's own share basis (ni/eps) is 1,522M = 4.5x = 3 x 1.5, i.e. already restated for the 2016 3:1 and 2017 3:2 bonuses. Only the 2024 3:2 remains, so K = 1.50, not 6.75. Corrected 2011-01-31: pe_now 5.49 -> 8.24, pe_need 8.50 -> 12.75, both far inside 60/35. The signal the claim says "drives the deep bucket" (2022-06-30, +591% net) uses fy2021, whose eps IS restated for the 2024 bonus: K = 1.00, zero error.

EXHIBIT 2 (FEDERALBNK) WRONG MECHANISM. K_eps = 1.00 (shs 1,710M = as-filed 171M x 5 x 2, fully on today's basis). pe_now 1.03 comes from the PRICE leg: 2013-08-30 bhavcopy close 256.15 vs charting 5.123 -> F_px = 50.0 where the true cumulative factor is 10. nse_charting_day double-adjusts FEDERALBNK by 5x before 2013-10-17. True pe = 5.14 - neither the stated 1.03 nor 1.03 x 6.75.

CLAIMED MECHANISM ADMITS NOTHING. K_eps > 1.1 for only 44/902 fully measured signals (HINDPETRO 22 @1.5, NMDC 10, IDEA 9 @1.66, WIPRO 3). Worst corrected pe_need 22.52 vs the 35 gate; worst corrected pe_now 16.51 vs the 60 gate. 0 of 902 signals flip either gate - the K_eps-corrected maxima equal the raw maxima (pe_now 25.01, pe_need 34.98) because the signals sitting nearest the gates are precisely the ones with K_eps = 1. (The one signal at pe_need 34.98 is 0.06% inside the gate: boundary coincidence, not this defect.)

ONE GENUINE EXCEPTION, NOT A CITED NAME. HDFCAMC had a real 1:1 action ex 2025-11-26 (bhavcopy 5,779 on 11-25 -> 2,679 on 11-26) that is MISSING from fmp.splits_calendar. Charting back-adjusted it (F_px 2.0 before, 1.0 after) while eps was not restated (N_eps = 213M = as-filed). That understates pe_now/pe_need by 2x for 19 signals / 7 episodes - the claim's mechanism, via a missing calendar record, for exactly one symbol. The other 12 flipped signals are charting adjustment errors, not eps: PERSISTENT F_px 4 vs true 2 (double-adjusted), STAR restated in eps but unadjusted in price, FEDERALBNK as above.

MATERIALITY. Correcting both legs (K = F_px/R_eps) removes 31/902 signals and 10/253 episodes. DEEP medAnnEx 12.6% -> 10.6% against shallow 6.4% -> 7.1%; DEEP medNet 75.8% -> 74.9%; beat 73% -> 73%. Portfolio hold-to-recovery: 10 slots +1.21pp -> +0.31pp vs NIFTYBEES, 20 slots -1.10pp -> -1.22pp. Conclusion (a) holds, (b) and (c) are reinforced, not moved. Substituting an FV-free measured estimate for the 221 FV-unresolved signals reproduces these numbers exactly (239 episodes, +0.31pp / -1.22pp) and is insensitive to how ambiguous events are classified; the +2.31pp 20-slot sign flip appears only under R=1 (eps never restated), the assumption the FV-free test refutes for 77% of events.

CARRIED FORWARD, SEPARATE FINDING, NOT MEASURED HERE: 160 of 1,599 ca_audit split events show the charting close JUMPING by the raw split factor on the ex-date. A forward walk crossing such a boundary books a FABRICATED recovery - FEDERALBNK's 2011-13 episodes hold a frozen target hi=10.02 while charting steps 6.69 -> 34.38 on 2013-10-17. fixed.py truncates the HIGH at these dates but does not stop walk() from crossing one, so it survives the corrected pipeline and deserves its own measurement.

audit.lens: portfolio — portfolio simulation (report.portfolio / variants.pf) and the bucket conclusion
audit.verdict_on_conclusion:
My lens overturns (a), destroys the stated evidence for (b) while strengthening its direction, and strongly supports (c) — but for reasons the write-up does not give.

(a) OVERTURNED, and harder than the doc's own mid-audit retraction. The retraction says +41.4% is "metric-fragile" and HINDPETRO-skewed. The truth is worse: HINDPETRO was never a winner. Its three deep episodes returned +65.3%, +76.9%, +64.0% on price against benchmarks of +54.8%, +103.4%, +27.1% — it LOST to the index on two of three. The +1956%/+1229%/+591% figures are a corrupt dividend field (F0). Remove the impossible rows and the DEEP bucket's mean excess goes +41.4% → −24.8%, statistically indistinguishable from the shallow band's −23.5%/−24.6%. There is no deep-entry edge to find.

(b) The stated evidence FAILS; the direction survives and gets stronger. "20 slots 9.16% vs NIFTYBEES 10.27%" — now billed in the rewritten doc as "the one headline number to trust" — is wrong in three directions at once: corrupt dividends inflate it by +2.3 to +3.8pp (F0), 36% idle zero-yield cash deflates it by 2.0 to 3.6pp (F3), and omitted real failures inflate it by 1.2pp (F2). Correctly specified, hold-to-recovery at 20 slots returns 5.35–6.87% against 10.27% — it loses to the index by 3.4 to 4.9pp, not 1.1pp. So the conclusion holds while the number offered as proof does not. Separately, its sign is a start-date coin flip: −1.10pp at the actual start, +2.57pp starting six months later (F6).

(c) SUPPORTED, strengthened, and the doc's reasoning should be replaced. "54 thin episodes, drawdown no better than the index" is the weak version. The strong version: every capital-weighted headline in the document is manufactured by a data bug (+12.04pp → +0.20pp); the portfolio sim contains zero survivorship correction despite the doc claiming it is "the behavioural truth" on exactly that question; drawdown on invested capital is −49%, not the reported −30%; and the sign of every headline flips within the start-date and fill-order noise. Nothing here is a safe alpha, and the "+4.37pp when diversified" fallback the rewrite now offers is −2.38pp once the dividends are sane.

findings.title: 36% of the book sits in zero-yield cash for 15.7 years because slots cap NAMES, not capital
findings.claim: alloc = eq/slots with eq marked before same-day entries cannot over-allocate — the `if cash < alloc*0.999: break` gate holds and there is no leverage bug. The defect is the opposite: the slot cap counts positions, so a holding down 80% still occupies a full slot while representing 20% of a slot's capital. The book structurally de-invests as losers sink, cash accrues from closed winners, and that cash earns exactly nothing while the benchmark is 100% invested. Entries are blocked by 'slots full' on 128 of 186 decision dates versus by 'cash short' on only 8, so this is a design artifact of the slot rule, not a funding constraint.
findings.direction: Biases AGAINST the rule. It is a material part of why the 20-slot book reads below the index.
findings.empirical: Recorded cash/equity every day. base20: mean cash 35.6%, median 40.5%, 79% of days above 20% cash, mean invested 64.4%. base10: mean cash 33.2%. Counterfactuals: cash at 6%/yr (realistic Indian liquid fund) base20 9.16%→11.14% (edge +0.87pp), base10 11.48%→13.34%; cash at the NIFTYBEES daily return base20 9.16%→12.75% (edge +2.48pp), base10 →16.13%, +36m/10 →24.94%, +36m/20 →17.83%. No-leverage check: min cash/equity across 60+ sims is exactly 0.000000. Scripts: scratchpad/audit/m1.py, m2.py.

Netting all three artifacts (no HINDPETRO + failures folded in + cash at index) gives base20 8.81% (edge -1.45pp) and +36m/10 11.35% (edge +1.08pp): the rule sits at the index, not above or meaningfully below it.

findings.title: Claim (d)'s mechanism is empirically false: deepest-first ranking does not produce the 10-vs-20-slot gap
findings.claim: RESULTS.md asserts the +12.04pp 10-slot result and the deep-bucket excess are 'the same thing' because rank_by='up' fills slots deepest-first, so '10 slots ≈ the deep bucket each month, while 20 slots dilutes into the shallow band'. The sort is coded correctly — up = -off/(1+off) is monotone in depth — but the stated mechanism does not exist. At 20 slots, reversing the sort to shallowest-first changes nothing. Selection almost never binds: the median decision date offers fewer candidates than there are free slots, so the book takes whatever exists. And 10-slot fills are predominantly shallow, not deep. The doc's conclusion ('not independent confirmation') happens to be right, but for a different reason — they are the same STOCK via the same data bug, not the same bucket.
findings.direction: Unclear for the rule; it invalidates the stated causal story and removes the only explanation offered for the 10-vs-20 divergence.

Under the base rule the effect REVERSES: at 10 slots shallow-first 13.53% beats deep-first 11.48%. Selection binds (more eligible candidates than free slots) on only 19% of dates at 10 slots and 10% at 20; median candidates available per date is 2 and 1 respectively; slots are entirely full on 47% and 20% of dates. Fill-depth histogram, share of fills at <=-35% off high: base5 60%, base10 52%, base20 35%, ts36_10 38%, ts36_20 24% — so 62% of the 10-slot/36m fills are shallow entries, against 20% deep in the episode sample. findings.title: Reported MDD understates invested-capital drawdown by ~19pp on the hold-to-recovery books
findings.claim: MDD is computed on the total equity curve, which is 36% unlevered cash. That dilutes drawdown mechanically and makes the base books look less risky than the index when the stock sleeve is far riskier. RESULTS.md claim #3 — 'Drawdown never improves on the index (-27.7% to -38.0% vs NIFTYBEES's -36.34%)' — is also internally false as written, since -27.66%, -29.75% and -31.30% all do improve on -36.34%.
findings.direction: Biases IN FAVOUR of the rule by understating risk. Supports conclusion (c)'s spirit while invalidating the figures used to argue it.
findings.empirical: Computed a flow-free invested-sleeve return series (per-position marks carried day to day, so entries and exits inject no artificial return) and took its drawdown. Reported vs sleeve MDD: base5 -37.13% vs -46.38%; base10 -31.30% vs -50.22%; base20 -29.75% vs -49.31%; +36m/10 -27.66% vs -31.07%; +36m/20 -35.09% vs -37.10%. Index -36.34%. DATA (confirmed by measurement): 58 of 5,884 priced dividend rows exceed 20% of the prevailing close — the claim's exact count, with the exact symbol concentration (HINDPETRO 21, CUPID 14, ARVIND 9, DRREDDY 7, CESC 4, plus ANGELONE/STAR/TATAINVEST 1 each). ROOT CAUSE — one correction to the claim's diagnosis, which does not rescue it. The claim frames this as an absolute rupee amount added to a back-adjusted series, implying a unit/basis mismatch. It is not that. Pulling `dividend` alongside `adjDividend` from FMP shows adjDividend is correctly split-adjusted on the same basis as the charting close (DRREDDY at a consistent 5x: 6.25->1.25, 18.0->3.6, 20.0->4.0; HINDPETRO 1972.40->1314.93 = exactly 1.50x for the 2017 1:2 bonus). The defect is vendor VALUE corruption in a small set of rows (DRREDDY's real FY18 dividend was Rs 20/share; FMP carries dividend=8638.20 / adjDividend=1727.64 — 86x. HINDPETRO's real FY21 was Rs 22.75; FMP carries 1972.40/1314.93 — 58x. The clean recent rows read correctly: HINDPETRO 2025-08-14 = 10.50, 2026-08-14 = 19.25). So the method is defensible and the field is poison. 1.4% of symbol-years carry an impossible yield (max 694.9%); dropping the 58 rows takes the max implied yield from 694.9% to 30.8%. The effect is fatal rather than noise precisely because those 1.4% of rows hold 25.4% of the value and sit in 8 names the result leans on.

DIRECTION: confirmed, favours the rule. One wording caveat — "the single reason ANY portfolio arm beats the index" is slightly overstated. finding.title: Claim (d)'s mechanism is empirically false: deepest-first ranking does not produce the 10-vs-20-slot gap

Selection almost never binds: the median decision date offers fewer candidates than there are free slots, so the book takes whatever exists. And 10-slot fills are predominantly shallow, not deep. On the pipeline that actually produces the published table, every sub-claim fails (numbers in empirical_check): selection binds on 94%/88% of decision dates, not 19%/10%; median free slots is 0 and the fill loop breaks on `slots` on 178 of 186 dates; reversing the sort at 20 slots moves hold-to-recovery −2.10 → −2.92pp and +36m −0.45 → −2.35pp, not "literally nothing"; 10-slot fills are 77% deep (≤−35%) against a 60%-deep pool, not 38%/"predominantly shallow". 3. THE SUBSTITUTE EXPLANATION IS THE DOC'S OWN. "Same STOCK via the same data bug" is the HINDPETRO `adjDividend` corruption, which is already RESULTS.md's stated explanation at HEAD (Retraction 1, final bullet: "the residue of the 'edge' was the HINDPETRO dividend corruption"). verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, not refuted — but it moves nothing, and half the claim is aimed at a document that no longer says that.

(1) Mechanism is real in CODE, and the claim's WHERE is stale in a way that does NOT save the study. report.py:121-128 and variants.py:86-92 are the superseded first pass that RESULTS.md explicitly disowns ("Do not quote their output"), and every figure the claim cites (-37.13/-31.30/-29.75/-27.66/-35.09, Calmar 0.81, "36% cash") comes from main.log/variants.log. But nodiv.py:85-88 — the file that produces every number in the current RESULTS.md — does the identical thing: `ev = cash + sum(marks)`, `mdd = (ev/maximum.accumulate(ev)-1).min()`. So the defect survives into the shipped numbers.

(2) Mechanism is real in DATA. I built a flow-free invested-sleeve return series on the current arms (per-position prev_val marks, so entries and exits inject no artificial return) and confirmed reported MDD = mean invested fraction x sleeve MDD to within 0.7pp on all three hold-to-recovery arms. Sleeve MDD is -45.87% to -60.82% against reported -32.30% to -59.72%. Independent validation: at 89% invested (+36m/10) reported and sleeve MDD converge (-59.72% vs -60.82%), and the gap scales with cash exactly as predicted. So the MDD column is the sleeve scaled by invested fraction, as claimed — the magnitude is larger on the current arms than on the retracted ones the auditor measured.

(3) The wording half persists, with different rows. The sentence quoted does not exist any more; RESULTS.md was rewritten at 13:53, after the audit at ~13:25. Its successor, point 2, carries the same error: "Drawdown is never better and is often far worse — −32% to −60% against the index's −36%". -32.30% (sanitised 10 slots) and -34.55% (sanitised 20 slots) both improve on -36.34%, and the doc quotes both two paragraphs earlier; -36.06% (sanitised DEEP/20) is a third. The five rows of the headline table are all genuinely worse than the index, so the table is directionally safe — only the cited range is wrong. Note the irony: fixing the dilution REPAIRS the sentence. On the sleeve basis 0 of 10 arms beat -36.34%; on a cash@index basis 0 of 6 do.

(4) Direction is as claimed — it flatters the rule — which means it runs against the document's own anti-rule verdict. Correcting it makes every arm look riskier.

(5) Conclusions. (a) NOT MOVED: on the sleeve basis deep is still the worst arm (DEEP/20 sleeve CAGR 10.66%, Calmar 0.19 vs base/20 12.71%, 0.22). (b) NOT MOVED BY THIS DEFECT: MDD carries no CAGR information and Calmar is near-invariant (reported 0.17-0.40 vs sleeve 0.19-0.42). (c) NOT MOVED, STRENGTHENED: true like-for-like drawdown is -46% to -61%, not -32% to -60%.

One thing I will not argue away, because I measured it and it points the other way: the cash-remuneration issue — a separate finding, already RESULTS.md limit #4 and the earlier lens's F2, not this claim — does flip the sign of (b)'s stated margin. 20-slot hold-to-recovery goes 8.16% as coded, 9.79% at 6% cash, 11.24% with idle cash in NIFTYBEES (+0.97pp); sanitised 9.46% / 11.01% / 12.41% (+2.14pp). The invested sleeve beats the index on raw CAGR. It is still not a risk-adjusted win at 20 slots (Calmar 0.25/0.30 vs 0.28, MDD -45.43%/-41.43% vs -36.34%), the hybrid is a different strategy from the rule as specified, and the later A21/A22 lens puts both-legs-clean h2r/20 at 8.35% before any cash credit. So (b) holds, but its margin rests on the cash convention, not on 2.10pp of signal.

Fix needed is documentation, not code: restate point 2 on a fully-deployed basis (-46% to -61% vs -36%), and put invested fraction and sleeve MDD in the table. I did not edit RESULTS.md — concurrent sessions are live on this tree and this was a refute task.
