finding.title: Every portfolio headline's sign is set by the start month and by fill-queue path dependence
finding.claim: Shifting the first decision date by one to twelve months — a free parameter with no economic content — moves the headline by more than the headline itself. The jackknife shows the same fragility in the cross-section: removing symbols that are not large winners costs 8-9pp, because their absence reshuffles which candidates reach a free slot. The 22.31% is one path through a 10-slot queue, not an estimate of an expected return.
finding.direction: Unclear — it flips both the pro-rule and anti-rule conclusions. It means neither headline is a measurement.
finding.empirical: Start-date sweep, +36m/10 across starts +0 to +12 months: CAGR 22.31, 22.69, 20.07, 20.55, 12.32, 12.39, 12.29, 13.71, 15.32% — edge +12.20pp down to +1.79pp, a 10.40pp CAGR spread, with a cliff between start+3 and start+4. base20: edge -1.10pp at start+0, -1.24, -0.97, -0.63, then +2.57pp at start+6 and +2.52pp at start+12 (CAGR 13.07% and 13.92% against the index's 10.27%) — conclusion (b)'s sign is a start-date artifact. base5: +8.06pp at start+0 but -2.80pp at start+6. Leave-one-symbol-out jackknife over all 98 symbols at +36m/10: HINDPETRO -12.14pp, then TECHM -9.21pp, BAJAJ-AUTO -8.53pp, M&MFIN -8.26pp, AXISBANK -8.25pp, NMDC -8.21pp — none of the latter five are outsized winners; 6 of 98 removals move CAGR more than 5pp, 14 move it more than 2pp, jackknife range 10.17% to 22.74%. Scripts: scratchpad/audit/m1.py, m2.py, m5.py, m6.py.
finding.magnitude: ±5 to ±12pp of CAGR from parameters with no economic content. Both conclusion (b) and the pro-rule headline reverse sign inside this noise.
finding.where: backtest/report.py l.82-87 (dates/fill_of built from DDATES[0]); main.py l.50-51; variants.py l.117-123

verdict.which_conclusion: None. (a) was already retracted before this claim and is now the LEAST fragile number in the study; (b) survives all 9 start dates and all 316 leave-one-out runs; (c) is reinforced. The only change earned is a wording one: RESULTS.md's 10-slot "+0.98pp / +2.53pp" is the single most favourable of nine start dates (median start +0.03pp / +1.66pp), which strengthens the "indistinguishable from noise" line it already carries.
verdict.reasoning:
NOT REFUTED AS A PHENOMENON — every number the auditor quotes reproduces exactly, and I confirmed the mechanism they only inferred. But the claimed severity ("material") and direction ("flips both conclusions") are refuted, for three measured reasons.

1. It is not a defect at the cited lines. report.py 82-87 is `dates=[x for x in nb_d if x>=DDATES[0]]` plus the `fill_of` map; main.py 50-51 is `for slots in (5,10,20)`; variants.py 117-123 is the arm loop. Starting the sim at the first decision date and filling on the next trading bar is the design, not an error. The benchmark is recomputed over the same shifted window at every start (b_cagr drifts 10.27% to 11.41% across +0..+12), so `edge` is window-matched and the comparison stays like-for-like. DDATES[0] is also not "a free parameter": it is the earliest date the data supports (2011 adjustment era + 400-bar history), not a knob anyone tuned. The finding is a statistical property of a path-dependent 10-20-slot sim with 26-64 closed trades. Its remedy is reporting a band, not patching code.

2. The quoted magnitudes are the already-identified F1 dividend defect wearing a different hat. On the superseded +36m/10, HINDPETRO is 1242 of 2384 realised equity units = 52.1% of all PnL on 3 trades. Dropping BAJAJ-AUTO — own PnL +9.6 units, 0.4% of realised — costs -8.54pp because HINDPETRO's fills fall 3 to 1 and its PnL 1242 to 75. Same for M&MFIN, AXISBANK, NMDC: every one of their 8-9pp deltas routes through HINDPETRO's fill count. The auditor is right that these are not outsized winners; the queue reshuffle is real. It is extreme only because one corrupt-dividend name is half the book's profit.

3. The fragility does not transfer to the shipped pipeline, and where it survives it points the wrong way for the claim. Porting `start_i` into the corrected sim (fixed.py MIN_BARS + real-CA fix, fixed_pf.py combined panel, nodiv.py dividend field untrusted), over 9 starts: base20 nodiv edge -4.93..-2.10pp, base20 sanitised -3.55..-0.81pp — ZERO sign flips in either, so the claim's specific assertion that conclusion (b)'s sign is a start-date artefact is false on the shipped numbers. deep20 (conclusion (a) as now stated, "deep is worst") spans just 1.07pp with 0 flips, the most start-robust figure in the study. The retracted 22.31%/+12.04pp becomes 8.72-12.35% CAGR / edge -1.99..+1.98pp, a 3.97pp spread, not 10.40pp. Decisively: start+0 is the BEST of nine starts for base20 (both dividend treatments), base10 nodiv and ts36_20 — every shift makes the rule look worse, never better. Corrected leave-one-out over 158 symbols gives 0/158 sign flips and 0 removals >2pp at 20 slots (worst TECHM -0.85pp), against the superseded 6 of 98 >5pp and a 10.17-22.74% range. The 9 flips that do occur (base10) all go from +0.98pp to negative.

The slot cap does bind on 160-171 of 174-186 decision dates at 20 slots, so queue path-dependence is a genuine mechanism — it is simply no longer attached to anything large enough to matter once no single name is 52% of PnL. Median leave-one-out impact: +0.000pp.

So: real, correctly diagnosed, honestly worth a reported band — and it moves nothing. "The 22.31% is one path, not an estimate" is true and was already conceded; RESULTS.md retracted that headline before this claim was filed and explicitly says of the surviving 10-slot arm that it "rests on 26 closed trades in 15.7 years and is indistinguishable from noise."
